1:1.headline: Why David could not get warm: age, a cut robe, or fear?
1:1.body: Radak and Ralbag say old age drains the body's natural heat, so clothes cannot help. Rashi records the sages' view that he was punished for cutting the corner of Saul's robe, or that the sight of the angel's sword chilled him.

sources.quote: והזקן כל זמן שהולך ומזקין החום הטבעי הולך וחסר
sources.says: Radak says that as an old man grows older, his natural heat keeps decreasing.

sources.quote: ידוע שהבגדים אינם מחממים כ"א במקרה מצד שמירתם שהאויר המקיף בגוף לא יקררהו
sources.says: Ralbag says clothes only warm by accident, by keeping the surrounding air from cooling the body.

sources.quote: כָּל הַמְבַזֶּה בְּגָדִים, אֵינוֹ נֶהֱנֶה מֵהֶם לַסוֹף, לְפִי שֶׁקָּרַע אֶת כְּנַף הַמְּעִיל לְשָׁאוּל
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: whoever shames clothes gets no benefit from them in the end, because David tore the corner of Saul's robe.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁרָאָה דָוִד אֶת הַמַּלְאָךְ עוֹמֵד בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וְחַרְבּוֹ בְּיָדוֹ, נִצְטַנֵּן דָּמוֹ מִיִּרְאָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi gives another midrash: when David saw the angel standing with his sword in hand, his blood went cold from fear.

1:2.headline: Sokenet: a warmer, a treasurer, or someone useful?
1:2.body: Rashi reads סכנת as one who warms, from the verb in 'one who splits wood is warmed by it'. Ralbag reads it as keeper of the stores, and Radak prefers 'one who is useful', which fits the cold that gripped the king.

sources.quote: סֹכֶנֶת. מְחַמֶּמֶת, וְכֵן: וּבוֹקֵעַ עֵצִים יִסָּכֶן בָּם
sources.says: Rashi says סכנת means warming, as in 'one who splits wood is warmed by it'.

sources.quote: ותהי לו סוכנת. ר"ל שומרת האוצרות
sources.says: Ralbag says סוכנת means a keeper of the stores.

sources.quote: והנכון בעיני שפירוש מועילה, כלומר, שיהיה למלך תועלת בה מפני הצנה אשר אחזתהו
sources.says: Radak says the right meaning is 'useful', so the king would benefit from her because of the chill that gripped him.

1:4.headline: 'Knew her' is a polite word for lying together
1:4.body: Metzudat Zion says ידעה is a polite word for lying with a woman. Rashi and Radak give two reasons the king did not: a virgin warms better, and the sages say a king may not take too many wives.

sources.quote: ידעה. הוא כינוי למשכב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ידעה is a word used in place of lying together.

sources.quote: שֶׁהַבְּתוּלָה יָפָה לְחַמֵּם מִן הַבְּעוּלָה. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ: מִשּׁוּם לֹא יַרְבֶּה לּוֹ נָשִׁים, וּכְבָר הָיוּ לוֹ שְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר
sources.says: Rashi says a virgin is better for warming than one who has been with a man, and the sages say he did not take her because a king must not have many wives, and he already had eighteen.

sources.quote: ורבותינו ז"ל פירשו שהיתה אסורה לו לבעלה משום לא ירבה לו נשים
sources.says: Radak says the sages explained that she was forbidden to him as a wife because a king must not take many wives.

1:6.headline: 'Bore him after Absalom' may mean 'raised him' that way
1:6.body: Radak says it simply means Haggith bore him after Absalom was born. Rashi and Ralbag say ילדה means raised, because Absalom's mother was a different woman: Adonijah was raised in Absalom's style.

sources.quote: חגית אם אדוניהו ילדה אותו אחר שילדה מעכה את אבשלום
sources.says: Radak says Haggith, Adonijah's mother, bore him after Maacah bore Absalom.

sources.quote: כְּלוֹמַר גִּדְּלַתּוֹ אַחַר תַּרְבּוּת שֶׁגִּדְלָה אִמּוֹ שֶׁל אַבְשָׁלוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says it means she raised him after the upbringing that Absalom's mother gave.

sources.quote: ואילו היה מענין הלידה היה ראוי שיהיו שניהם מאם אחת
sources.says: Ralbag says if it meant birth, both would have had to be from one mother, so it means raising.

1:9.headline: 'En Rogel' is the fuller's spring, named for foot-trampling
1:9.body: Targum Jonathan renders עין רגל as 'the fuller's spring', as Rashi and Radak report. The fuller treads woolen clothes with his feet, which is why he is called רוגל.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: עֵין קַצְרָא, הוּא כּוֹבֵס, שֶׁמְּתַקֵּן בִּגְדֵי צֶמֶר בְּרַגְלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says Targum Jonathan renders it 'the fuller's spring', one who fixes woolen clothes with his feet.

sources.quote: ונקרא הכובס בעבור זה רוגל לפי שהוא משפשף בגדים ברגליו
sources.says: Radak says the launderer is called רוגל because he rubs clothes with his feet.

1:14.headline: 'I will fill your words': complete them, or follow them?
1:14.body: Metzudat David and Targum Jonathan read ומלאתי as completing and confirming her words. Ralbag allows that, or that Nathan will follow her words, as in 'he followed the Lord fully'.

sources.quote: בעוד שתדברי עם המלך, אבוא גם אני להשלים דבריך
sources.says: Metzudat David says that while you speak with the king, I will come too and complete your words.

sources.quote: וַאֲקַיֵם יַת פִּתְגָמָיְכִי
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it 'and I will confirm your words'.

sources.quote: אשלים מה שיחסר בהם או ירצה בזה שימשך לדבריה כטעם כי מלא אחרי ה'
sources.says: Ralbag says it means I will complete what is missing in them, or that he will follow her words, as in 'he fully followed the Lord'.

1:18.headline: 'And now' or 'and you'? Radak says scribes got this word wrong
1:18.body: Radak says many scribes wrote this word with an aleph, 'and you', but the exact books and the Masorah have an ayin, 'and now'. Metzudat David reads 'and now' as something being done now that you do not know about.

sources.quote: רבים מהסופרים טעו בזאת המלה וכתבו אות' באל"ף
sources.says: Radak says many of the scribes made a mistake with this word and wrote it with an aleph.

sources.quote: אבל ברור הוא אצלינו כי הוא ועתה בע' מפי ספרים המדוייקים ומפי המסורת
sources.says: Radak says it is clear to him that it is ועתה with an ayin, from the exact books and from the Masorah.

sources.quote: ועתה. דבר הנעשה עתה, הנה לא ידעת מזה
sources.says: Metzudat David says ועתה means something being done now, which you do not know about.

1:24.headline: 'You said it' is really a question: 'Did you say it?'
1:24.body: Rashi and Radak say אתה אמרת is asked in surprise. Metzudat David says the question's ה is left out: 'Did you say Adonijah will reign?'

sources.quote: אַתָּה אָמַרְתָּ. בִּתְמִיָּה
sources.says: Rashi says אתה אמרת is said in astonishment.

sources.quote: אתה אמרת. על דרך תמיהה
sources.says: Radak says אתה אמרת is said as a question of surprise.

sources.quote: אתה. תחסר ה״א השאלה, והוא כמו האתה אמרת
sources.says: Metzudat David says the question-hey is missing, so it means 'did you say'.

1:31.headline: 'Long live the king' may mean life of the soul
1:31.body: Metzudat David and Radak read יחי as life of the soul, forever in the world to come, since David was near death. Radak adds that Targum Jonathan renders it 'may he endure', where it usually says 'may he succeed'.

sources.quote: יחי אדוני. רוצה לומר: בחיי הנפשות, וזה שאמרה לעולם
sources.says: Metzudat David says יחי means life of the souls, which is why she said forever.

sources.quote: פי׳ חיי נפש לעולם הבא כי בעולם הזה קרוב היה למיתה
sources.says: Radak says it means life of the soul in the world to come, because in this world he was near death.

sources.quote: וכן תרגום יונתן יתקיים וכל שאר יחי המלך תרגם יצלח
sources.says: Radak says Targum Jonathan renders it 'may he endure', while elsewhere it renders 'long live the king' as 'may he succeed'.

1:33.headline: 'Gihon' is a flowing spring: kings are anointed where water flows
1:33.body: Rashi says גחון is the Shiloach spring, and that kings are anointed at a spring as a sign that their reign will flow on. Metzudat David says the same: it is a good sign that his reign will last like a stream.

sources.quote: הוּא מַעְיַן הַשִּׁלּוֹחַ, מִכָּאן שֶׁאֵין מוֹשְׁחִין אֶת הַמְּלָכִים אֶלָּא עַל הַמַּעְיָן, סִימָן שֶׁתִּמָּשֵׁךְ מַלְכוּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the Shiloach spring, and that kings are anointed only at a spring, as a sign that their reign will continue.

sources.quote: גיחון. שם נחל, והוא השלוח, כן תרגם יונתן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says גיחון is the name of a stream, the Shiloach, as Targum Jonathan renders it.

sources.quote: אל גיחון. לסימן טוב, שתמשך מלכותו כנחל
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a good sign that his reign will go on like a stream.

1:38.headline: The Kerethites and Pelethites: archers and slingers, or the Urim and Tummim?
1:38.body: Targum Jonathan renders them 'archers and slingers', as Rashi and Metzudat Zion report. Rashi adds the sages' reading, the Urim and Tummim, and Ralbag says they were the Sanhedrin.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: וְקַשָּׁתַיָּא וְקַלָּעַיָּא. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ: אוּרִים וְתֻמִּים
sources.says: Rashi says Targum Jonathan renders them archers and slingers, and the sages said they are the Urim and Tummim.

sources.quote: והכרתי והפלתי. תרגם יונתן: וקשתיא וקלעיא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Targum Jonathan renders them archers and slingers.

sources.quote: והכרתי והפלתי. הם היו סנהדרין כמו שקדם
sources.says: Ralbag says the Kerethites and Pelethites were the Sanhedrin.

1:39.headline: Which 'tent' did the anointing oil come from?
1:39.body: Rashi and Metzudat David say it is the tent David pitched in his city for the Ark, where the anointing oil was kept. Radak says it is the Tent of Meeting, then at Gibeon, and that Zadok went or sent there for the oil.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָאָרוֹן נָתוּן בְּעִיר דָּוִד, וּצְלוֹחִית שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה לִפְנֵי הָאָרוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says the Ark was in the city of David, with the flask of anointing oil before it.

sources.quote: אשר נטה דוד בעירו, להכניס בו הארון, ושם היה שמן המשחה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the tent David pitched in his city to bring in the Ark, and the anointing oil was there.

sources.quote: מאהל מועד כי שם היה שמן המשחה ואף על פי שאהל מועד היה בזמן ההוא בגבעון הלך שם צדוק או שלח להביאו
sources.says: Radak says it is from the Tent of Meeting where the oil was, and though that tent was at Gibeon then, Zadok went or sent to bring it.

1:51.headline: 'If he kills' in an oath means 'that he will not kill'
1:51.body: Metzudat David says אם ימית here means he will not kill, as if the oath's penalty falls on him if he does. Targum Jonathan renders it 'that he will not kill his servant', and Radak says it means 'swear to me that he will not kill me'.

sources.quote: אם ימית. רצה לומר: שלא ימית, וכאלו אמר שיהיה עליו עונש שבועה אם ימית
sources.says: Metzudat David says אם ימית means that he will not kill, as if the penalty of the oath is on him if he kills.

sources.quote: דְלָא יְקַטֵיל יַת עַבְדֵיהּ בְּחַרְבָּא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it 'that he will not kill his servant with the sword'.

sources.quote: מזה שאני מפחד תמיד ומסופק בו ישבע לי שלא ימיתני
sources.says: Radak says that because I am always afraid and unsure of him, let him swear to me that he will not kill me.

10:1.headline: Famous 'for the name of God': what does that mean?
10:1.body: Metzudat David says she heard that Solomon's wisdom came from God, not from human nature. Radak says his wisdom was used for God's sake, unlike the magicians of other lands, and Ralbag offers both readings.

sources.quote: שמעה אשר חכמתו איננה מטבע האנושי, כי אם מה׳ היתה לו
sources.says: Metzudat David says she heard that his wisdom was not from human nature but came to him from God.

sources.quote: כי רוב החרטומים והאשפים המתעסקים בחכמות החצונות אין מלאכתם לשם ה' וחכמת שלמה היתה לשם ה'
sources.says: Radak says most magicians and sorcerers do not work for God's sake, but Solomon's wisdom was for God's sake.

sources.quote: ויהיה הרצון באמרו לשם ה' בעבור שם ה' או יהיה הרצון בזה שהיא שמעה שמעו שכל מה שהיה עושה היה עושה לשם ה'
sources.says: Ralbag gives two readings: because of God's name, or that she heard everything he did was done for God's sake.

10:1.headline: Why she tested him with riddles
10:1.body: Malbim says some riddles cannot be solved by human cleverness alone, like Samson's riddle about the lion and the honey. So riddles were the right test of a wisdom that came from God.

sources.quote: כי א"א בחכמה אנושית לבד להגיד כל החדות שלפעמים ענינם נעלם כמו חדתו של שמשון
sources.says: Malbim says human wisdom alone cannot answer every riddle, since sometimes the meaning is hidden, as with Samson's riddle.

sources.quote: ותבא לנסותו בחידות. כלומר בדברים סתומים בחכמה
sources.says: Radak says riddles are matters of wisdom that are hidden.

10:2.headline: She came with great wealth, or with a great army?
10:2.body: Metzudat Zion and Ralbag read חיל as wealth and goods. The Targum renders it as large camps, and Malbim says she brought a heavy guard because she came overland through the desert.

sources.quote: בחיל. עושר וקנינים, כמו (ירמיהו יז ג) חילך וכל אוצרותיך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חיל means wealth and possessions, as in Jeremiah 17:3.

sources.quote: הרצון בו נכסים וקניינים רבים
sources.says: Ralbag says it means many goods and possessions.

sources.quote: בְּמַשִׁרְיַן סַגִיאִין לַחֲדָא
sources.says: The Targum says she came with very large camps.

sources.quote: למעלתה הלכה דרך המדבר לכן באת בחיל כבד לשמרה בדרך
sources.says: Malbim says that, as befits her rank, she went by the desert road, so she came with a heavy force to guard her.

10:5.headline: His burnt offerings, or his stairway up to the Temple?
10:5.body: Rashi and Radak say עלתו here is Solomon's way up: the passage he built from his palace to the Temple. Radak notes the Targum reads it as the burnt offerings he brought there.

sources.quote: דֶּרֶךְ מָבוֹא שֶׁהֵכִין מִבֵּיתוֹ לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁהָיָה עוֹלֶה בוֹ לְבֵית ה'
sources.says: Rashi says it is the passage Solomon prepared from his house to the Temple, which he went up by.

sources.quote: מעלות שעשה לעלות מביתו לבית המקדש היו בנויים בחכמה ובאומנות וכן בדברי הימים ועלייתו אבל יונתן תרגם ועלתיה דמסיק בית מקדשא דה'
sources.says: Radak says these were the steps from his house to the Temple, called 'his ascent' in Chronicles, but the Targum reads 'his burnt offering that he brought up'.

10:12.headline: A floor, a railing, or pillars? A word found only here
10:12.body: Chronicles calls the same thing מסלות, a path, so Rashi reads מסעד as paving. Metzudat David says it was the walkway with railings to lean on, from סעד, 'support', while Radak says it was pillars holding up the ceilings.

sources.quote: וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים כְּתִיב: מְסִלּוֹת לְבֵית ה', לְכָךְ אֲנִי אוֹמֵר, הַמִּסְעָד הַזֶּה לְשׁוֹן רִצְפָּה
sources.says: Rashi says Chronicles writes 'paths for the house of God', so he takes מסעד to mean a floor.

sources.quote: וכאן נקרא מסעד, לפי שהיה לו כעין מעקה מפה ומפה, להיות העולה נשען ונסעד בהם
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is called מסעד because it had a kind of railing on both sides for the one going up to lean on.

sources.quote: ובדברי הימים מסלות ופירושו עמודים לסמיכת התקרות
sources.says: Radak says it means pillars that hold up the ceilings.

10:13.headline: What she wanted from Solomon was wisdom
10:13.body: The verse says Solomon gave her everything she desired. Rashi says this gift was nothing but teaching her wisdom, and Radak agrees that what she asked for were words of wisdom.

sources.quote: נְתִינָה זוֹ אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא לִמּוּד חָכְמָה
sources.says: Rashi says this giving was only the teaching of wisdom.

sources.quote: את כל חפצה אשר שאלה. בדברי חכמה
sources.says: Radak says what she asked for was words of wisdom.

10:15.headline: Traders named for scouting, like the spies
10:15.body: Metzudat Zion says התרים are traders who scout for cheap goods, from the verb used for the spies who 'scouted the land'. Ralbag says they were the big merchants who searched far countries for goods.

sources.quote: הם הסוחרים הקטנים המחפשים ומרגלים אחר סחורה לקנות במקום הזול, והוא מלשון (במדבר יג טו) לתור את הארץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are small traders who search out goods to buy cheaply, from 'to scout the land' in Numbers 13.

sources.quote: קרא התרים הסוחרים הגדולים שהם תרים וחוקרים על דבר הסחורות בקצות הארץ
sources.says: Ralbag says the התרים are the great merchants who search out goods at the ends of the earth.

10:15.headline: Kings of Arabia, or kings bound to him by pledge?
10:15.body: Metzudat Zion says these are the Arab kings. Rashi follows the Targum and reads ערב as in ערבות, a pledge: these were kings under his protection who relied on him.

sources.quote: מלכי הערב. הם הערביים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are the Arabs.

sources.quote: וְכָל מַלְכֵי סוּמְכְוָתָא, לְשׁוֹן עֲרֻבָּה, הַמְּלָכִים שֶׁהָיוּ בַעֲרֻבָּתָן וְסוֹמְכִין עָלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says, following the Targum, these are kings under his guarantee who leaned on him.

10:16.headline: A big shield that wraps around three sides
10:16.body: Rashi and Malbim say a צנה covers a man on three sides, while a מגן covers only one. Rashi points to Psalm 5:13, 'you surround him with favor like a צנה'.

sources.quote: צִנָּה. מַקֶּפֶת אֶת הָאָדָם מִשְּׁלשָׁה רוּחוֹתָיו, וְהוּא שֶׁאָמַר בְּסֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים: כַּצִּנָּה רָצוֹן תַעְטְרֶנּוּ
sources.says: Rashi says a צנה surrounds a person on three sides, as in Psalms 'like a צנה you surround him with favor'.

sources.quote: הצנה מקיף מג' רוחות והמגן מרוח א'
sources.says: Malbim says the צנה covers three sides and the מגן one side.

10:16.headline: 'Slaughtered gold' means gold drawn out like wax
10:16.body: The word looks like 'slaughtered'. Metzudat Zion and Radak say it means drawn out, as in 'their tongue is a drawn arrow', so this was gold pure enough to stretch like wax.

sources.quote: שחוט. נמשך, כמו (ירמיהו ט ז) חץ שחוט לשונם, ורוצה לומר: זהב טוב נמשך כשעוה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שחוט means drawn out, as in Jeremiah 9:7, meaning good gold that draws out like wax.

sources.quote: אין שחוט אלא משוך וכן חץ שחוט לשונם והיה זהב טוב מאד שהיה נמשך כשעוה
sources.says: Radak says שחוט only means drawn out, and this was very good gold that stretched like wax.

sources.quote: זָהָב שָׁחוּט. הוּא רַךְ וְנוֹחַ לְהֵרָקַע
sources.says: Rashi says it is soft gold that is easy to beat thin.

10:22.headline: Ships of Tarshish: the Targum says Africa
10:22.body: Rashi and Radak follow the Targum, which calls Tarshish 'Africa'. Malbim reports that Abarbanel took it to be Carthage in North Africa, and was then puzzled how ships from the Red Sea could get there.

sources.quote: אֳנִי תַרְשִׁישׁ. (תַּרְגּוּם:) סְפִינַת אַפְרִיקָא
sources.says: Rashi gives the Targum: a ship of Africa.

sources.quote: תרשיש. תרגם יונתן אפריקא
sources.says: Radak says the Targum renders Tarshish as Africa.

sources.quote: הרי"א חשב כי תרשיש היא העיר קארטאגא בצפון אפריקא על יד ים התיכון, ועי"כ הרבה לתמוה איך הלכו אניות מעציון גבר
sources.says: Malbim says Abarbanel thought Tarshish was Carthage in North Africa, and so wondered how ships went there from Ezion-geber.

11:2.headline: 'Surely' they will turn you, or 'lest' they turn you?
11:2.body: אכן usually means surely, and Radak reads it that way. He notes that the Targum turns it into a warning instead: lest they turn your heart.

sources.quote: באמת יטו לבבכם כמו שאומר כי יסור את בנך מאחרי וי"ת דילמא יטעון לבכון
sources.says: Radak says it means 'truly they will turn your heart', and that the Targum renders it 'lest they lead your heart astray'.

11:5.headline: Solomon 'went after' idols by not stopping his wives
11:5.body: The verse says Solomon followed the gods of Sidon and Ammon. The commentators say he did not worship them himself. He let his wives do it and said nothing, so the verse blames him.

sources.quote: על שלא מיחה בנשיו ההולכות, מעלה עליו הכתוב כאילו הלך אחריהם
sources.says: Metzudat David says that because he did not stop his wives, the verse counts it as if he went after the idols himself.

sources.quote: הרצון שהניח לנשיו הצידוניות והעמוניות לעבוד אלהיהם והעלים עיניו מהם
sources.says: Ralbag says it means he let his Sidonian and Ammonite wives serve their gods and looked away.

11:7.headline: Solomon 'built' the altar by letting his wives build it
11:7.body: The verse says Solomon built a shrine for Chemosh. Rashi and Ralbag say his wives built it, but it is called his because he could have stopped them and did not.

sources.quote: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא מִחָה בְּנָשָׁיו, נִקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi, citing the rabbis, says that because he did not protest against his wives, it is called by his name.

sources.quote: ולזה אז יבנה שלמה במה שהוא כאילו בנאה אחר שהניח נשיו לבנותה
sources.says: Ralbag says it is as if Solomon built it, since he let his wives build it.

11:11.headline: 'God said to Solomon': through a prophet, not face to face
11:11.body: The verse says God spoke to Solomon. Radak and Maimonides say the warning came through a prophet, most likely Ahijah of Shiloh.

sources.quote: על ידי נביא והוא אחיה השילוני
sources.says: Radak says God spoke through a prophet, Ahijah of Shiloh.

sources.quote: שזה בלי ספק איום שנאמר לו על ידי נביא
sources.says: Maimonides says this was surely a threat told to Solomon by a prophet, Ahijah or another.

11:14.headline: Here the 'satan' is a human enemy, Hadad of Edom
11:14.body: שטן means an adversary. Here it is a person, Hadad, a prince of Edom whom God raised against Solomon. Malbim says the point was to correct Solomon through human hands.

sources.quote: מקטרג, להסית אנשיו ללחום בו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means an accuser who stirred his men to fight Solomon.

sources.quote: ע"י שהקים שטן לשלמה והוכיחהו בשבט אנשים עד שהתנחם על מעשיו
sources.says: Malbim says God raised an enemy to correct Solomon with human blows until he regretted what he had done.

11:26.headline: 'Raised a hand' against the king: a revolt, or a public rebuke?
11:26.body: The phrase usually means a revolt. Rashi says Jeroboam rebuked Solomon in public. Radak says his revolt was that he spoke against the king without fear.

sources.quote: וַיָּרֶם יָד בַּמֶּלֶךְ. הוֹכִיחוֹ בָּרַבִּים
sources.says: Rashi says it means Jeroboam rebuked the king in public.

sources.quote: מרד בו שדבר בו ולא ירא ממנו
sources.says: Radak says he rebelled by speaking against the king without fear of him.

11:27.headline: The Millo: an open square where the people gathered
11:27.body: Radak says the Millo was an open place in Jerusalem where the people came together. He takes the name from מלא, which he reads as a gathering.

sources.quote: והיה רחבה להתאסף שם העם מענין קראו אחריך מלוא שהוא ענין אסיפה
sources.says: Radak says it was a square for the people to gather, named from a word meaning a gathering.

11:30.headline: Twelve pieces, or twelve tears in one cloak?
11:30.body: קרעים can mean torn pieces or the tears themselves. Metzudat David notes that twelve tears would leave thirteen pieces.

sources.quote: י״ב חתיכות או, קרעים ממש, ובי״ב קרעים יש י״ג חתיכות
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means twelve pieces, or twelve actual tears, which would make thirteen pieces.

11:36.headline: David's 'lamp', or David's 'yoke' of rule?
11:36.body: ניר here may stand for נר, a lamp. Metzudat David says a king is called that because he gives light. Rashi reads it as rule, from the word for a yoke.

sources.quote: נִיר. מֶמְשָׁלָה, וְ'נִיר' לְשׁוֹן 'עֹל'
sources.says: Rashi says it means rule, and that ניר is a word for a yoke.

sources.quote: ויקרא המלך כן, על שם שמשפיע ומאיר
sources.says: Metzudat David says a king is called a lamp because he gives out light.

sources.quote: ניר בחיר"ק כמו בצר"י כמו שאמר ערכתי נר למשיחי
sources.says: Radak says ניר is the same word as נר, lamp, as in 'I have set a lamp for my anointed'.

11:37.headline: Rule over all you desire, or rule over your desires?
11:37.body: God promises Jeroboam he will reign over all his soul desires. Metzudat David reads it as wide rule. Malbim reads it as a condition: first rule your own desires, then rule the people.

sources.quote: למשול ממשל רב
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means to rule widely.

sources.quote: אם ימלוך על כחות נפשו ותאוותיו שיכנעו תחת משמעת השכל אז הוא הראוי למלוך על העם
sources.says: Malbim says that if he rules his own desires so they obey his reason, then he is fit to rule the people.

12:1.headline: Shechem, a place the midrash says was marked for trouble
12:1.body: Israel met in Shechem, in Ephraim, Jeroboam's tribe, and not in Jerusalem. Radak adds a midrash: at Shechem Dinah was abused, at Shechem Joseph was sold, and at Shechem David's kingdom split.

sources.quote: ובדרש שכם מזומן לפורענות בשכם ענו את דינה בשכם מכרו את יוסף בשכם נחלקה מלכות בית דוד
sources.says: Radak cites a midrash that Shechem is set aside for disaster: Dinah was abused there, Joseph was sold there, and the kingdom of David's house split there.

sources.quote: שכם היה משבט אפרים
sources.says: Radak notes that Shechem belonged to the tribe of Ephraim.

sources.quote: אבל שכם היתה לראש יוסף ומתנגדת ליהודה
sources.says: Malbim says Shechem was the head city of Joseph and stood against Judah.

12:2.headline: Did Jeroboam stay in Egypt or come back? Same letters, both
12:2.body: Here וישב means he stayed in Egypt. Chronicles uses the same letters to say he returned from Egypt. Malbim says both are true: he stayed until the people sent for him, and then came back.

sources.quote: וישב ירבעם במצרים ובדה"ב (י' ב') כתוב וישב ירבעם ממצרים
sources.says: Malbim notes that Kings has Jeroboam stay "in Egypt" while Chronicles has him return "from Egypt".

sources.quote: תחלה עת שמע הדבר לא חזר ממצרים כי לא ידע תוכן הדברים
sources.says: Malbim says that when he first heard the news he did not come back, since he did not know what was going on.

sources.quote: עם כל זאת ישב במצרים, ולא חזר מעצמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says that even so he stayed in Egypt and did not return on his own.

12:6.headline: Rehoboam asks the elders "how" to answer, not "what" to do
12:6.body: With the elders he asks איך, "how". With the young men, in verse 9, he asks מה, "what". Malbim says this shows he had already decided to refuse the people, and only wanted help with the wording.

sources.quote: וז"ש איך אתם נועצים ולא אמר כמ"ש אח"ז מה אתם נועצים, שמלת מה, היא שאלה על גוף העצה
sources.says: Malbim says he asked "how" and not "what", because "what" asks about the decision itself.

sources.quote: רק רצה להתיעץ באיזה אופן ידחם מעל פניו
sources.says: Malbim says he only wanted advice on the way to turn them away.

12:11.headline: The "scorpions" here are thorny whips, not the stinging animal
12:11.body: עקרבים usually means scorpions. Rashi, Metzudat Zion, Ralbag and Radak say here it is a rod or plant with thorns that sting like a scorpion. Rehoboam threatens to beat harder than his father did with plain whips.

sources.quote: שֶׁעוֹקְצִין כְּעַקְרָב
sources.says: Rashi names a thorny plant in the local language and says its thorns sting like a scorpion.

sources.quote: בעקרבים. מין קוצים, כמו (יחזקאל ב ו) ואל עקרבים אתה יושב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עקרבים is a kind of thorn, as in Ezekiel.

sources.quote: שבטים אשר בהם קוצים שנוקבים ומכאיבים
sources.says: Ralbag says they are rods with thorns that pierce and hurt.

sources.quote: ועקרבים קשים מהם שהם עוקצים בקוצים שבהם
sources.says: Radak says עקרבים are harsher than whips, because they sting with their thorns.

12:16.headline: "See to your house, David": his family, or the Temple?
12:16.body: Plainly the tribes mean: see what is left for you to rule. Rashi, and a midrash Radak cites, read "your house" as the Temple Solomon built: keep it for yourself. Targum Jonathan reads it as "rule over the people of your house".

sources.quote: ראה ביתך. כלומר ראה מי נשאר עמך ועל איזה בית תמלוך כי לא על בית ישראל
sources.says: Radak says it means: see who is left with you and what house you will rule, since it will not be the house of Israel.

sources.quote: ובדרש ראה ביתך דוד זה בית המקדש
sources.says: Radak cites a midrash that "your house" is the Temple.

sources.quote: בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁבָּנִיתָ, לְךָ לְבַדְּךָ יִהְיֶה
sources.says: Rashi says it is the Temple you built, and it will be yours alone.

sources.quote: כְּעַן מְלוֹךְ עַל אֱנַשׁ בֵּיתָךְ דָוִד
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "now rule over the men of your house, David".

12:16.headline: Back to your tents, Israel: David's house was built from them
12:16.body: The cry sets Israel's tents against David's house. Malbim says the tribes left their tents to build David's house, so if they go back to their tents, he has no house. Targum Jonathan says "to your cities", since the tents are their homes.

sources.quote: ימליץ שבית דוד נבנה מאהלי ישראל, שהם נטשו אהליהם ובנו את ביתו
sources.says: Malbim says the verse hints that David's house was built from Israel's tents, which they left to build his house.

sources.quote: ואם ישובו אל אהליהם אין לו בית
sources.says: Malbim says that if they go back to their tents, he has no house.

sources.quote: גְבַר לְקִרְוָךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "each man to your cities, Israel".

12:20.headline: "Judah alone" also counts Benjamin, its smaller neighbor
12:20.body: The verse says only Judah stayed with David's house, yet the next verse names Benjamin too. Radak and Metzudat David say Benjamin is counted inside Judah, because Jerusalem lay between the two tribes.

sources.quote: כבר כתבנו כי שבט בנימין בכלל שבט יהודה כי ירושלם בין שניהם היתה
sources.says: Radak says the tribe of Benjamin is included in Judah, since Jerusalem lay between them.

sources.quote: ואף בני בנימין נכללו עמהם, על כי ירושלים עיר המלוכה היתה לנחלה לשניהם
sources.says: Metzudat David says Benjamin is included with them, since Jerusalem, the royal city, belonged to both.

sources.quote: לרבוי שבט יהודה ביחס אל שבט בנימן לא חשב שבט בנימן
sources.says: Ralbag says Judah was so much larger than Benjamin that Benjamin was not counted on its own.

12:25.headline: Jeroboam "built" Shechem: he fortified a city that already stood
12:25.body: Shechem was a living city: Israel had just gathered there. So Radak and Ralbag say "built" here means he strengthened its walls and made it fit for a king. The same goes for Penuel.

sources.quote: ועוד כי שם התקבצו ישראל להמליך רחבעם ודאי עיר בנויה היתה אלא פי' ויבן שחזק חומות העיר ובנה בו היכל מלך
sources.says: Radak says Israel gathered there to crown Rehoboam, so it was surely a standing city; "built" means he strengthened its walls and built a palace there.

sources.quote: ר"ל שחזק בנינו והוסיף על העיר בדרך שהיה ראוי להיות עיר מלוכה
sources.says: Ralbag says he strengthened its buildings and added to the city so it would suit a royal city.

12:27.headline: Why kill Jeroboam? In the Temple court only David's kings sit
12:27.body: Radak, citing the sages, asks why the people would kill him. The answer: in the Temple court only kings of David's line may sit. Seeing Rehoboam seated and Jeroboam standing, the people would take Jeroboam for a rebel.

sources.quote: ובדברי רז"ל מאי והרגוני גמירי דאין ישיבה בעזרה אלא למלכי בית דוד בלבד
sources.says: Radak cites the sages: why "they will kill me"? Because there is a tradition that only kings of David's house may sit in the Temple court.

sources.quote: כיון דחזו ליה לרחבעם דיתיב ואנא קאימנא סברי מורד במלכות הוא
sources.says: Radak goes on: when they see Rehoboam sitting and Jeroboam standing, they will think he is a rebel against the king.

sources.quote: אֵין יְשִׁיבָה בָּעֲזָרָה אֶלָּא לְמַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד בִּלְבַד, וְיִהְיֶה הוּא יוֹשֵׁב וַאֲנִי עוֹמֵד
sources.says: Rashi says only David's kings may sit in the Temple court, so Rehoboam would sit while Jeroboam stood.

12:28.headline: רב לכם: enough of going up, or too far to go?
12:28.body: Radak reads רב לכם as "enough for you": stop going up to Jerusalem from now on. Targum Jonathan and Ralbag read it as "the road is too long for you". Either way Jeroboam presents the calves as sparing them trouble.

sources.quote: רב לכם מעלות ירושלם. די לכם עד עתה הניחו מהיום ואילך מעלות ירושלם
sources.says: Radak says it means: enough for you until now; from today on, stop going up to Jerusalem.

sources.quote: סַגִיאָה לְכוֹן אָרְחָא מִלְמֵסַק לִירוּשְׁלֵם
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "the road is too long for you to go up to Jerusalem".

sources.quote: ואמר הנה רב לכם הדרך מעלות כולכם בירושלם כי ישיגכם לאות רב
sources.says: Ralbag says Jeroboam told them the road to Jerusalem was too long for all of them and would wear them out.

12:28.headline: Jeroboam repeats the very words said over Aaron's golden calf
12:28.body: "Here is your God, Israel, who brought you up from Egypt" echoes what was said at the calf in the desert. Radak and Metzudat David say Jeroboam used those words on purpose: as with Aaron's calf, God's presence was supposed to rest on it.

sources.quote: פיתה אותם לאמר אשר השכינה תשרה על עגלי הזהב, וכאשר טעו מאז בהעגל שעשה אהרן לזה אומר בהלשון הזה עצמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says he lured them by saying God's presence would rest on the golden calves, and since they once erred with Aaron's calf, he used the very same words.

sources.quote: הלא אהרן עשה לישראל עגל להשרות השכינה בו במקום משה
sources.says: Radak says Jeroboam told them that Aaron made a calf for God's presence to rest on, in place of Moses.

sources.quote: לפיכך אמר אלה אלהיך ישראל אשר העלוך מארץ מצרים כמו שאמר בעגל המדבר
sources.says: Radak says that is why he said these words, just as was said of the calf in the desert.

12:29.headline: Bethel means "house of God", and Jeroboam used that
12:29.body: Radak says Jeroboam put a calf in Bethel because Jacob had said of this place, "this will be the house of God". Ralbag says it was well known that God's presence had rested there on Jacob.

sources.quote: בבית אל לפי שאמר להם זה המקום גם כן נבחר כמו ירושלם כי יעקב אבינו אמר על המקום הזה יהיה בית אלהים
sources.says: Radak says Jeroboam told them this place was chosen too, like Jerusalem, since Jacob said of it that it would be a house of God.

sources.quote: להתפרסם הענין שכבר שרת' שם שכינה ליעקב
sources.says: Ralbag says he chose it because it was known that God's presence had rested there on Jacob.

12:31.headline: Priests "from the ends of the people", or from its thorns
12:31.body: מקצות means from anywhere among the people, whoever came. Radak says that could be the highest or the lowest. He adds that the sages heard קוצים, "thorns", in the word: Jeroboam's priests came from the thorns of the people.

sources.quote: מקצות העם. כמו ומקצה אחיו מן הגדולים או מן הפחותים ובדברי רבותינו ז"ל מן הקוצים שבעם
sources.says: Radak says it means from among them, either the great or the lowly, and that the sages read it as "from the thorns among the people".

sources.quote: מקצות העם. ממקצותם, יהיה מי שיהיה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means from any of them, whoever it might be.

12:33.headline: Written "besides", read "from his heart": two readings of one word
12:33.body: The text is written מלבד, "besides", but read מלבו, "from his heart". Radak says the written form means he made up feasts besides God's feasts. He cites the sages: Jeroboam made up his own Sabbaths and holidays too.

sources.quote: מלבו. מלבד כתיב ר"ל אשר בדא מלבד מועדי ה'
sources.says: Radak says the word is written מלבד, meaning he made up a feast apart from God's appointed times.

sources.quote: ובדברי רז"ל אף שבתות וימים טובים בדא ירבעם מלבו
sources.says: Radak cites the sages that Jeroboam also made up Sabbaths and holidays from his own heart.

14:3.headline: A rare word for dry, speckled bread brought as a gift
14:3.body: Rashi says נקדים is grain roasted dry in an oven. The Metzudat Zion says it is dry bread with spices, called 'dotted' because the spices fleck it.

sources.quote: מִין קְלָיוֹת, מְיַבְּשִׁין בְּתַנּוּר וְעוֹשִׂין אוֹתָן קֶמַח
sources.says: Rashi says it is a kind of roasted grain, dried in an oven and ground into flour.

sources.quote: על כי המה מנוקדים ומנומרים ממראה התבלין
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says it is dry spiced bread, named for being dotted with the spices.

14:4.headline: His eyes 'stood up': they stopped moving, and he was blind
14:4.body: קמו usually means 'rose'. Here it means the eyes stood still: a seeing eye moves, but a blind eye stays fixed in one place.

sources.quote: לפי שדרך העין להתנענע בעת הראות
sources.says: The Metzudat David says a seeing eye moves, but when sight is gone it stands fixed in one place.

sources.quote: לעת הזקנה תיבש הלחות ויקומו יתרי העין
sources.says: Radak explains it as the drying of the eye in old age.

14:5.headline: The root for 'recognize' here means making yourself unrecognizable
14:5.body: מתנכרה shares its root with הכרה, recognizing. Radak says it means the reverse: she made herself a stranger no one would know.

sources.quote: מתנכרה. הפך ההכרה
sources.says: Radak says the word means the opposite of being recognized.

sources.quote: עושה עצמה כנכרית, כאלו אינה אשת ירבעם
sources.says: The Metzudat David says she acted like a stranger, as if she were not Jeroboam's wife.

14:7.headline: God 'raised' Jeroboam: lifted him in rank, or set him apart
14:7.body: Maimonides uses this verse to show that רם can mean high in rank, not high in place. The Metzudat Zion and Targum Jonathan read it as 'I set you apart', like a portion set aside.

sources.quote: ובמשמעות רום המעלה, כלומר הגדולה והכבוד והעוז
sources.says: Maimonides says רם can mean height of rank, and cites this verse for that sense.

sources.quote: הרמותיך. מלשון תרומה, ורצה לומר: הפרשתיך
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion reads it from תרומה, a portion set aside, meaning 'I separated you'.

sources.quote: חֲלַף דְאַפְרִישְׁתָּךְ מִגוֹ עַמָא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan translates it 'because I separated you from among the people'.

14:10.headline: 'One who urinates on a wall', or one who keeps wisdom inside
14:10.body: The plain sense is every male, and the Sages said even a dog. Targum Jonathan reads משתין as משית, 'sets', so it means a man who keeps knowledge set in the walls of his heart.

sources.quote: הוא הזכר, כי עושה קלוח ומשתין בקיר
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the phrase means the male.

sources.quote: אפילו הכלב שדרכו להשתין בקיר
sources.says: Radak brings the Sages' reading, even the dog, as an overstatement, and Targum Jonathan's reading of one who sets counsel in his heart.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: יָדַע מַדָּע, מֵשִׁית בְּקִירוֹת לִבּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi cites Targum Jonathan: one who knows, who sets things in the walls of his heart.

14:10.headline: 'Shut in and left free': people, or money and cattle?
14:10.body: Rashi reads the pair as people: those with someone to back them and those with no one. Radak's father read them as goods: money locked in a storehouse and cattle left in the field.

sources.quote: עָצוּר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַחֲזִיק יָד
sources.says: Rashi says עצור is one who has someone to support him, and עזוב one who has no one.

sources.quote: פירש עצור על הממון שהוא עצור באוצר ועזוב המקנה שהוא עזוב בשדה
sources.says: Radak gives his father's reading: money shut in the treasury and cattle left in the field.

14:10.headline: Galal: dung swept away, a grinding tooth, or a whirlwind
14:10.body: Some read הגלל as dung, cleared out until none is left. The Sages read it as the tooth, which grinds food away completely, and Ralbag as a whirlwind that sweeps away whatever it meets.

sources.quote: הגלל. הצואה, כמו (יחזקאל ד טו) גללי האדם
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says it means dung, as in Ezekiel.

sources.quote: גלל זה השן רוצה לומר כמו שמבער השן המאכל עד תומו
sources.says: Radak brings the Sages' view that galal is the tooth, which clears food away completely, and also the view that it is dung.

sources.quote: ולפי דעתי שהרצון בו כאשר יבער הרוח המגלגל
sources.says: Ralbag gives the Sages' tooth reading, then his own: a whirling wind that sweeps away all in its path.

14:13.headline: The verse never says what the one good deed was
14:13.body: The verse says only that 'a good thing' was found in this son of Jeroboam. The Sages fill it in: he left the post where his father set him to stop pilgrims, and went up for the festival himself.

sources.quote: שֶׁבִּטֵּל מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ, שֶׁהוֹשִׁיבוֹ אָבִיו שׁוֹמֵר
sources.says: Rashi says he left the guard post where his father placed him to stop people going up for the festival, and went up himself.

sources.quote: לא גלה הכתוב מה דבר טוב נמצא בו
sources.says: Radak notes the verse does not reveal the good deed, and brings the Sages' view that he removed the guards his father set on the roads.

14:14.headline: 'And what, even now?': a puzzling phrase read two ways
14:14.body: Rashi, following Targum Jonathan, reads it as 'those born today and those born from now on' will all be cut off. Radak reads it as 'what is this trouble, even now?': it is small next to the troubles still coming on Israel.

sources.quote: הַנּוֹלָדִים לוֹ הַיּוֹם, וַאֲשֶׁר עֲתִידִין לְהִוָּלֵד לוֹ מֵעַתָּה
sources.says: Rashi, citing Targum Jonathan, says it means those born to him today and those to be born from now on.

sources.quote: נקלה היא צרה זו כי יותר ויותר יבאו על ישראל צרות
sources.says: Radak says this trouble is light, because more and more troubles will come on Israel.

14:15.headline: A curse that hides a blessing: a reed bends but stays rooted
14:15.body: Israel will sway like a reed in water. Radak brings the Sages: even in a curse the image is kind, since a reed sways but is not torn from its place.

sources.quote: אפילו בשעת קלקלה המשיל' לקנה במים אמר שהוא נד ואינו נעקר ממקומו
sources.says: Radak brings the Sages: even in a time of rebuke he compared Israel to a reed in water, which sways but is not uprooted.

sources.quote: אשר לרוב רכותו, יתנודד במעט רוח
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the reed is so soft that it sways in the slightest wind.

14:25.headline: Shishak was named for his longing for Solomon's throne
14:25.body: Rashi brings a midrash that Shishak was Pharaoh Necho. He was called שישק because he longed (שוקק) all his life for the ivory throne of Solomon, and now he came and took it.

sources.quote: וְנִקְרָא שִׁישַׁק, עַל שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹקֵק וּמִתְאַוֶּה כָּל יָמָיו לְכִסֵּא הַשֵּׁן
sources.says: Rashi says he was called Shishak because he yearned all his days for Solomon's ivory throne.

14:26.headline: 'He took everything': Rashi says it means the throne
14:26.body: After the treasures, the verse adds 'and he took it all'. Rashi reads 'it all' as one thing: Solomon's throne, dearer than everything else.

sources.quote: אֶת הַכִּסֵּא, הֶחָבִיב מִן הַכֹּל
sources.says: Rashi says 'everything' means the throne, which was dearer than all the rest.

15:4.headline: A lamp for David, or a field that keeps bearing?
15:4.body: God gave David a ניר in Jerusalem. Metzudat Zion reads it as a lamp, meaning a kingdom that stays lit. Ralbag reads it as plowed land that bears crops, meaning children who carry on the line.

sources.quote: ניר. כמו נר, ורוצה לומר: מלכות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ניר is like נר, a lamp, and means kingship.

sources.quote: ניר הוא הארץ הנעבדת באופן שיהיו הצמחים אשר בה פרים
sources.says: Ralbag says ניר is farmed land whose plants bear fruit, so God gave David offspring to rule in Jerusalem.

sources.quote: יְהַב יְיָ אֱלָהֵיהּ לֵיהּ מַלְכוּ
sources.says: The Targum translates 'God gave him a kingdom'.

15:10.headline: Asa's 'mother' was really his grandmother
15:10.body: Maacah was named as Abijam's mother a few verses back. Here she is called Asa's mother too. Commentators say she was his grandmother, called mother because she raised him.

sources.quote: ולא היתה אם אסא אלא אם אבים אביו
sources.says: Radak says Maacah was not Asa's mother but his father Abijam's, and a grandmother can be called mother.

sources.quote: אם אביו היתה, ולפי שהיתה מגדלתו, אמר אמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says she was his father's mother, called his mother because she raised him.

15:12.headline: Idols named after dung
15:12.body: The word for idols here, גלולים, sounds like גלל, dung. Metzudat Zion says the name shows the idols are as disgusting as filth.

sources.quote: העבודת גלולים המאוסים כגלל וצואה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the idols are called this because they are loathsome like dung and filth.

15:22.headline: 'No one was free', not even a new bridegroom
15:22.body: נקי usually means clean or innocent. Here it means exempt. Rashi and Radak tie it to the Torah's law that a new husband is נקי, free from war duty, for a year. Asa called up even him.

sources.quote: אֲפִלּוּ חָתָן מֵחֶדְרוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: נָקִי יִהְיֶה לְבֵיתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says even a bridegroom was taken from his room, though the Torah calls him free for his household.

sources.quote: אפי' חתן שנאמר עליו נקי יהיה לביתו שנה אחת
sources.says: Radak says the same: even a bridegroom, who is free for one year.

17:15.headline: 'Days' that the Sages read as a full year
17:15.body: The verse says they ate for 'days'. The Metzudat Zion brings the Sages' reading that this means a whole year, and Ralbag also says they ate from it for one year.

sources.quote: ימים. אמרו רבותינו ז״ל: שנה
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the Sages read 'days' as a year.

sources.quote: וזכר ששנה אחת אכלו מזה
sources.says: Ralbag says they ate from it for one year.

17:20.headline: The Targum turns Elijah's complaint against God into a plea
17:20.body: Elijah asks God, 'Have You done harm to this widow?' Targum Jonathan softens it to 'let no harm come to her, and let her son not die'.

sources.quote: לָא יִתְבָּאֵשׁ לָהּ וְלָא יְמוּת בְּרָהּ
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it 'let no harm come to her and let her son not die'.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם ברם על ארמלתא די אנא דר עמה לא יתבאש לה ולא ימות ברה
sources.says: Radak quotes the Targum's softer wording.

17:21.headline: Elijah 'measured himself' against the boy's body
17:21.body: ויתמדד comes from מדה, measure: Elijah stretched out on the child, matching him limb to limb. The Metzudat David says it was to pass life from his body into the boy's, and Radak adds it may also have warmed him.

sources.quote: מִלְּשׁוֹן מִדָּה, נִשְׁתַּטַּח עָלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says the word comes from measure: he stretched himself out on the boy.

sources.quote: וכאילו מדד עצמו למדת הילד, ולהשפיע החיות מאיבריו אל אברי הילד
sources.says: The Metzudat David says he fitted himself to the child's size to pass life from his limbs to the boy's.

sources.quote: כי עשה כן להנשים עליו ולחממו בחום הטבעי היוצא מפניו ומבשרו
sources.says: Radak says he may also have done it to breathe on the boy and warm him with his own body heat.

18:10.headline: How could Ahab make foreign kingdoms swear?
18:10.body: Obadiah says Ahab made every nation swear Elijah was not there. Some taught that Ahab ruled the whole world. Radak and Ralbag reject that: he asked as a friend, not as their king.

sources.quote: ומה שאמר והשביע את הגוי והממלכה דרך אהבה ובקשה לא בדרך יראה ושררה
sources.says: Radak says he made them swear by friendly request, not by fear and rule.

sources.quote: לא כדברי האומר שמלך בכפה
sources.says: Radak rejects the view that Ahab ruled the whole world.

sources.quote: אך לא מלך אחאב בכלל העולם
sources.says: Ralbag says Ahab did not rule the whole world.

18:26.headline: Why does Elijah have to hand them the bull?
18:26.body: The prophets of Baal chose their own bull, yet the verse says Elijah 'gave' it to them. Rashi brings a midrash: the bull ran from them to Elijah, refusing to be offered to an idol. Radak calls that far from reason and reads it simply.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה נִשְׁמַט מֵהֶם, שֶׁלֹּא יִקָּרֵב לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וּבָרַח לוֹ תַּחַת כְּנָפָיו שֶׁל אֵלִיָּהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the bull slipped away so as not to be offered to an idol and fled to Elijah's protection.

sources.quote: פירוש נתן להם בדברו שאמר להם בחרו לכם הפר האחד
sources.says: Radak says Elijah gave it to them by his words, when he told them to choose a bull.

sources.quote: ויש בדברי אגדה דברים רחוקים מן השכל
sources.says: Radak says the midrash here has things far from reason.

18:26.headline: Maimonides on why they thought Baal would answer
18:26.body: Maimonides says the prophets of Baal believed star powers flowed into their statues. They thought the statues could then speak and reveal things. That is why they cried 'Baal, answer us'.

sources.quote: וטענו שכוחות הכוכבים שופעים על הפסלים האלה כך שאותם פסלים מדברים ומבינים ומשכילים
sources.says: Maimonides says these idol worshippers claimed the stars' powers flowed into the statues, so the statues spoke and understood.

sources.quote: אלה היו נביאי הבעל ונביאי האשרה הנזכרים אצלנו
sources.says: He says these were the prophets of Baal and Asherah mentioned in the Bible.

18:26.headline: The Baal prophets 'limp' around their altar
18:26.body: This is the verb Elijah used for the people in verse 21. Radak reads it as limping back and forth like men in pain. Rashi brings the Aramaic, 'they acted wildly': they danced around the altar, as their worship required.

sources.quote: ופשוטו עשו עצמם כפסחים וכואבים הולכים ושבים על המזבח
sources.says: Radak says in its plain sense they made themselves like lame men in pain, going back and forth at the altar.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: וְאִשְׁתַּטּוּ, הָיוּ מְרַקְּדִין כְּמִשְׁפָּטָן עַל מִזְבְּחוֹתָם
sources.says: Rashi says the Aramaic means they acted wildly, dancing on their altars as was their custom.

18:27.headline: Baal is 'on the way': traveling, or in the bathroom?
18:27.body: Elijah says perhaps Baal has a דרך, a journey. Radak reads it plainly: he has gone off on some business. Rashi reads it as a crude joke: Baal has gone to relieve himself.

sources.quote: וְכִי דֶרֶךְ לוֹ. לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא
sources.says: Rashi says 'he has a way' means he went to the toilet.

sources.quote: וכי דרך לו. או הלך לו בדרך לעסק מעסקיו
sources.says: Radak says it means he went on the road for some business.

18:30.headline: Elijah 'healed' the broken altar
18:30.body: The verse says Elijah healed the altar. Radak and Metzudat David say the word for healing is borrowed for rebuilding, as Nehemiah speaks of healing Jerusalem's wall. Rashi adds that he brought God's altar back into Israel's hearts.

sources.quote: בא על דרך השאלה, לומר לשון רפואה על תיקון בנין הנהרס
sources.says: Metzudat David says the word for healing is borrowed for repairing a ruined building.

sources.quote: דרך השאלה אמר לשון רפואה לבנות הריסת הבנין וכן כי עלתה ארוכה לחומת ירושלם
sources.says: Radak says healing is used for rebuilding, as in 'healing came up to the wall of Jerusalem'.

sources.quote: וְהִזְכִּיר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת מִזְבַּח ה' עוֹלֶה עַל לִבָּם
sources.says: Rashi says he reminded Israel so that God's altar would come back to their minds.

18:31.headline: Why recall Jacob's new name before the contest
18:31.body: Elijah builds with twelve stones and recalls that God renamed Jacob Israel. Metzudat David says the name means 'you struggled with God and with men and won'. Elijah too would win, over the false gods and their prophets.

sources.quote: כי שרית עם אלהים ועם אנשים ותוכל
sources.says: Metzudat David says the name was given because 'you struggled with God and with men and prevailed'.

sources.quote: ולהזכיר זכות ישראל אביהם, שגם הוא כמוהו ינצח אלהים אחרים
sources.says: He says Elijah recalled their father Israel's merit, so that he too would overcome other gods.

sources.quote: שיהיה למעלה מן המזלות ומושל אף על המלאכים
sources.says: Malbim says the name means Israel stands above the stars and rules even over angels.

18:34.headline: Four jars, three times: twelve, like the tribes
18:34.body: Elijah has four jars poured, then again, then a third time. Radak counts twelve jars in all, matching the twelve stones and the twelve tribes.

sources.quote: ושלשה פעמים ארבעה הם שנים עשר כדי מים כטעם שנים עשר אבנים למספר שבטי בני ישראל
sources.says: Radak says three times four makes twelve jars of water, for the same reason as the twelve stones: the number of the tribes.

sources.quote: שלשו. שפכו פעם שלישית
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means pour a third time.

18:36.headline: 'By Your word' I broke the rule on altars
18:36.body: Offerings outside the Temple were forbidden in Elijah's time. Rashi says Elijah means: I built this altar by Your command. Radak says he wanted no one to call the fire his own sorcery.

sources.quote: שֶׁהִקְרַבְתִּי בַּבָּמָה בִּשְׁעַת אִסּוּר הַבָּמוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says Elijah offered on a local altar at a time when such altars were forbidden.

sources.quote: וטעם ובדברך שלא יאמרו מדעתי עשיתי כל מה שעשיתי
sources.says: Radak says he said 'by Your word' so they would not say he did all this on his own.

18:37.headline: Why does Elijah say 'answer me' twice?
18:37.body: The Aramaic, which Rashi brings, reads the two calls as answer me with fire, and answer me with rain. The sages read the second as: answer me so they will not call it magic. Radak says the doubling simply adds force.

sources.quote: עֲנֵנִי בָּאֵשׁ, עֲנֵנִי בַּמָּטָר, כָּךְ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן
sources.says: Rashi says the Aramaic translation reads it as answer me with fire, answer me with rain.

sources.quote: עֲנֵנִי שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ מַעֲשֵׂה כְשָׁפִים הֵם
sources.says: Rashi brings the sages: answer me so they will not say it is sorcery.

sources.quote: הכפל לחזק כמו שהוא בכל מקום שאין לו טעם אחר
sources.says: Radak says the doubling is for emphasis, as everywhere there is no other reason.

18:37.headline: Did God turn their hearts away, or will He turn them back?
18:37.body: Elijah says 'You turned their heart backward'. Rashi reads it as blame: You let them stray, though You could have held them. Metzudat David and Saadia Gaon read it as a hope: their heart was turned away, and now You will turn it back.

sources.quote: נָתַתָּ לָהֶם מָקוֹם לָסוּר מֵאַחֲרֶיךָ, וּבְיָדְךָ הָיָה לְהָכִין לְבָבָם אֵלֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says God gave them room to turn from Him, though it was in His hand to set their hearts toward Him.

sources.quote: עבר במקום עתיד, ורצה לומר: בהנס הזה תסבב אליך את לבם, אשר היה עד הנה אחורנית
sources.says: Metzudat David says the past tense stands for the future: through this miracle You will turn their heart, which was turned away until now, back to You.

sources.quote: פירש הגאון רב סעדיה לבם שהיה אחורנית תסב אותו אליך עתה אם תענני
sources.says: Radak brings Saadia Gaon: their heart, which was turned back, You will turn to You now if You answer me.

18:46.headline: A one-time verb for tying up one's robe to run
18:46.body: וישנס appears only here. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say it means girding, with no parallel. Rashi says it shows haste, like a warrior getting ready. Ralbag says Elijah bound himself tight so the hard running would not hurt him.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ וַיֶּאֱזֹר, וְאֵין לוֹ דִמְיוֹן, וְאַף הוּא לֹא בָּא אֶלָּא לְלַמֵּד לְשׁוֹן זֵרוּז
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'he girded', has no parallel, and comes to teach haste.

sources.quote: ענין חגורה, ואין לו דומה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means girding and has no parallel.

sources.quote: שחגר מתניו בדרך שיתכן לו לרוץ בזולת נזק באבריו הפנימיים
sources.says: Ralbag says he girded his waist so he could run without harm to his inner organs.

19:3.headline: Elijah "saw", or Elijah "was afraid"? Radak argues for saw
19:3.body: The letters וירא can be read "he saw" or "he was afraid". Some commentators read "afraid". Radak rejects that on grammar, and points to Targum Jonathan, which says "he saw": Elijah saw he was in danger.

sources.quote: ראה עצמו בסכנה והלך ונמלט אל נפשו והמפרשים וירא כמו ויירא לא ידעתי למה ועוד כי לא יתכן מדרך הדקדוק
sources.says: Radak says Elijah saw himself in danger and fled; some read the word as "he feared", but Radak does not see why, and the grammar does not allow it.

sources.quote: וַחֲזָא וְקָם וַאֲזַל לְשֵׁיזָבָא נַפְשֵׁיהּ
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "and he saw, and rose, and went to save his life".

sources.quote: וירא. ראה עצמו בסכנה
sources.says: Metzudat David says he saw himself in danger.

19:3.headline: "He went to his soul": saving his life, or his spirit?
19:3.body: וילך אל נפשו is literally "he went to his soul". Metzudat David and Targum Jonathan read it as going to save his life. Malbim reads it as going off alone to work on his own soul, since his miracles had not changed the people.

sources.quote: אל נפשו. בעבור למלט נפשו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means in order to save his life.

sources.quote: וַאֲזַל לְשֵׁיזָבָא נַפְשֵׁיהּ
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "and he went to save his life".

sources.quote: ואחר שראה שכל הנפלאות שעשה לא פעלו, ראה כי אין לו עסק להשלים את העם, ולכך קם וישב ללכת אל השלמת נפשו
sources.says: Malbim says that once Elijah saw his wonders had done nothing, he saw he had no more work improving the people, and set out to perfect his own soul.

19:4.headline: "No better than my fathers": Radak sees a hint Elijah is Pinchas
19:4.body: Elijah says he is no better than his fathers, who died. Radak says this suggests he had already lived longer than they did. He takes it as support for the view that Elijah and Pinchas were the same man.

sources.quote: נראה כי ארכו ימיו יותר מימי אבותיו וזה ראיה לאומר פנחס זה אליהו
sources.says: Radak says it seems Elijah had lived longer than his fathers, which supports the one who says Pinchas is Elijah.

sources.quote: כי לא טוב הוא מאבותיו שיזכה מפני זה לאורך הנפלא מן החיים
sources.says: Ralbag says Elijah meant he was not better than his fathers, that he should earn a wondrously long life.

19:5.headline: "One" rotem: a lone bush, or an angel in disguise?
19:5.body: The verse says again that he slept under "one" rotem. Radak says the word shows it was the only shelter in that desert, and barely enough. Malbim reads it as a second, larger tree, which was really the angel in the form of a tree.

sources.quote: להודיע כי הרותם היה יחידי ולא מצא באותו המדבר מחסה אחר שישכב שם אלא אותו רותם לבדו ובדוחק היה יכול לחסות תחתיו
sources.says: Radak says it tells us the tree stood alone: he found no other shelter in that desert, and could barely shelter under it.

sources.quote: לא מצא שנים (רתמים) יחד, לחסות בצילם כל אורך הגוף
sources.says: Metzudat David says he did not find two trees together to shade his whole body.

sources.quote: אבל הרותם השני הזה לא היה רותם באמת רק מלאך שנדמה לו כרותם
sources.says: Malbim says this second tree was not really a tree but an angel that looked to him like one.

19:8.headline: Forty days on one meal: how this differs from Moses
19:8.body: Moses went forty days and ate nothing. Radak points out that Elijah went "on the strength of that meal": the food stayed in his body and fed him all forty days. Malbim instead likens the two: the holy food refined Elijah's body as Moses' was.

sources.quote: לא היה זה כנס משה רבינו כי בו נאמר ארבעים יום וארבעים לילה לחם לא אכל ומים לא שתה ולא אמר שעמד בכח האכילה
sources.says: Radak says this was not like Moses' miracle: of Moses it says he ate no bread and drank no water for forty days, not that he lived on the strength of a meal.

sources.quote: על פי נס, לא נתעכלה במעיו כל הזמן ההוא
sources.says: Metzudat David says that by a miracle the food was not digested in him all that time.

sources.quote: וילך נדמה בזה למשה רבו שנזדכך גופו
sources.says: Malbim says in this Elijah resembled Moses his teacher, whose body was refined.

19:9.headline: "The cave": the same rock cleft where Moses stood
19:9.body: The verse says "the cave", as if it were known. Rashi, Metzudat David and Radak say it is the cleft of the rock on Sinai where God set Moses, which the Aramaic translation calls "the cave of the rock".

sources.quote: הִיא נִקְרַת צוּר שֶׁעָמַד בָּהּ משֶׁה
sources.says: Rashi says it is the cleft of the rock where Moses stood.

sources.quote: שעמד בה משה, וכמו שנאמר (שמות לג כב): ושמתיך בנקרת הצור, ותרגומו: במערת טנרא
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is where Moses stood, as in "I will put you in the cleft of the rock", which the Targum renders "in the cave of the rock".

sources.quote: מערה היתה בהר סיני ועליה נאמר ושמתיך בנקרת הצור
sources.says: Radak says there was a cave on Mount Sinai, and of it God said "I will put you in the cleft of the rock".

19:10.headline: Elijah's "zeal" is also vengeance, like Pinchas
19:10.body: קנא קנאתי means "I have been very zealous". Metzudat Zion explains it as "I took vengeance", and links it to the same words in Numbers 25. Radak says this zeal, killing Baal's prophets, is what drove Elijah to flee.

sources.quote: קנא קנאתי. נקם נקמתי, וכן (במדבר כה יא) בקנאו את קנאתי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means "I took vengeance", as in "when he was zealous with my zeal" in Numbers.

sources.quote: הקנאה שקנאתי לשם ה' והרגתי נביאי הבעל
sources.says: Radak says it means the zeal Elijah showed for God's name when he killed the prophets of Baal.

sources.quote: אותה הקנאה גרמה לי לצאת ממקומי לברוח מפני איזבל ולבא פה
sources.says: Radak says that zeal made Elijah leave his place, flee from Jezebel and come here.

19:12.headline: A "still small voice": a sound made of sound and silence
19:12.body: דממה means silence, so קול דממה is "a voice of silence". Metzudat David and Ralbag say it was a quiet voice, as if made of sound and silence together. Targum Jonathan, cited by Rashi, has "the voice of those who praise in a whisper".

sources.quote: דממה. ענין שתיקה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says דממה means silence.

sources.quote: קול חשאי כאלו היא מורכבת מקול ומשתיקה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it was a quiet voice, as if made of voice and silence.

sources.quote: קול נמוך מהש"י כאילו הוא מורכב מהקול והשתיקה
sources.says: Ralbag says it was a low voice from God, as if made of sound and silence.

sources.quote: קַל דִמְשַׁבְּחִין בַּחֲשָׁאִי
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "the voice of those who praise in a whisper".

19:15.headline: "Anoint Hazael" means appoint him; no oil is meant
19:15.body: Elijah never anointed Hazael or Jehu. Radak and Metzudat David say "anoint" here means appoint to high office, a word taken from the anointing of Israel's kings. Radak notes the same use for the patriarchs and for Cyrus.

sources.quote: לפי שמנוי המלוכה או הגדולה הוא ע"י משיחה ברוב נאמר למנוי אף על פי שאינו ע"י משיחה בלשון משיחה
sources.says: Radak says that since kings and leaders are mostly appointed by anointing, the word is used for any appointment, even without oil.

sources.quote: וכן אמר על האבות אל תגעו במשיחי וכן למשיחו לכורש
sources.says: Radak says the patriarchs are called "my anointed" in the same way, and so is Cyrus.

sources.quote: הלשון הזה יורה על מינוי הגדולה, והושאל ממשיחת מלכי ישראל, שהיתה משיחה ממש
sources.says: Metzudat David says the word means appointing to high office, borrowed from the anointing of Israel's kings, which was real anointing.

sources.quote: והנה אליהו לא משח את חזאל ולא יהוא
sources.says: Radak notes that Elijah anointed neither Hazael nor Jehu.

19:16.headline: "A prophet in your place": God did not want Elijah's accusations
19:16.body: Plainly, Elijah had asked to die, so he must leave a successor, says Radak. Rashi, and the midrash Radak cites, read it as a rebuke: God does not want a prophet who argues the case against His children.

sources.quote: אִי אֶפְשִׁי בִּנְבִיאוּתְךָ, מֵאַחַר שֶׁאַתָּה מְלַמֵּד קָטֵּיגוֹרְיָא עַל בָּנַי
sources.says: Rashi says God means: I do not want your prophecy, since you argue the case against My children.

sources.quote: כיון שאתה רוצה להסתלק מן העולם שאמרת רב עתה ה' קח את נפשי צריך שתניח נביא תחתיך
sources.says: Radak says that since Elijah wanted to leave the world, as he said "take my life", he must leave a prophet in his place.

19:17.headline: "Elisha will kill"? Rashi finds only the forty-two boys
19:17.body: Elisha was a prophet, not a soldier. Rashi says the only deaths we find him causing are the forty-two boys killed by bears. Radak gives two other readings: his warnings went unheeded and enemies killed the people, or raiders came when he died.

sources.quote: לֹא מָצִינוּ שֶׁהֵמִית אֶלָּא אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁנַיִם יְלָדִים עַל יְדֵי הַדֻּבִּים
sources.says: Rashi says we find he killed only forty-two children, through the bears.

sources.quote: כי בהוכיחו אותם ולא היו שומעים אליו ולא היו שבים מדרכם הרעה האויבים יבואו עליהם והרגום וכאילו הוא היה ממית אותם
sources.says: Radak says that when Elisha warned them and they did not listen or turn back, enemies came and killed them, so it is as if he killed them.

sources.quote: או פי' ימית אלישע במותו כי במות אלישע באו גדודי ארם ומואב בארץ
sources.says: Radak also says it may mean at his death, since when Elisha died, raiders from Aram and Moab came into the land.

19:19.headline: Plowing with the twelfth pair: a sign of the twelve tribes
19:19.body: Elisha was plowing behind the last of twelve pairs of oxen. Radak says the detail is told as a sign: Elisha would be set over the twelve tribes of Israel as their prophet. Ralbag adds that it shows how rich Elisha's father was.

sources.quote: והספור הזה להורות כי מצאו בי"ב והיה אות כי יהיה ממונה על י"ב שבטי ישראל לנביא ולמזהיר
sources.says: Radak says the story tells that Elijah found him with the twelfth pair, a sign that he would be set over the twelve tribes of Israel as prophet.

sources.quote: ואחשוב שזכר זה להעיד כי אבי אלישע היה עשיר מאד
sources.says: Ralbag thinks the detail is there to show that Elisha's father was very rich.

19:19.headline: Elijah throws his cloak: a silent sign of the prophet's call
19:19.body: Metzudat Zion says the אדרת was a fine cloak worn by prophets. Metzudat David says throwing it hinted that Elisha would be a prophet and wear one too. Radak says Elijah gave only a sign, without words, trusting Elisha to understand.

sources.quote: באדרתו. מלבוש חשוב מיוחד לנביאים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it was a fine garment special to prophets.

sources.quote: השליך עליו קצת מאדרתו, לרמזו שיהא נביא לה׳
sources.says: Metzudat David says Elijah threw part of his cloak on him to hint that he would be a prophet of God.

sources.quote: עשה לו סימן שילך אחריו ולא אמר לו בפי' כי ידע שיבין כי מה' יהיה נביא
sources.says: Radak says Elijah gave him a sign to follow without saying it outright, since he knew Elisha would understand he was to be God's prophet.

19:21.headline: בשלם: he cooked "for them", the people or the oxen?
19:21.body: Dunash and Menachem read בשלם as "he cooked for them", the people, and Radak and Metzudat Zion agree, with the ם standing for "to them". Rashi reads it as one word, with "them" meaning the two oxen: he cooked their own meat.

sources.quote: בִּשֵּׁל לָהֶם אֶת הַבָּשָׂר, כָּךְ פֵּרְשׁוּ דוֹנַ"שׁ וּמְנַחֵם
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash and Menachem explained it as "he cooked the meat for them".

sources.quote: בִּשְּׁלָם לִשְׁנֵי הַשְּׁוָרִים אֶת הַבָּשָׂר שֶׁלָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi himself says it means he cooked, for the two oxen, their own meat.

sources.quote: בשלם. בשל להם, רוצה לומר: להעם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means he cooked for them, that is, for the people.

sources.quote: ומ"ם בשלם במקום להם
sources.says: Radak says the ם of בשלם stands for "to them".

2:2.headline: 'Be a man': act grown up, or master yourself?
2:2.body: David tells young Solomon to be a man. Metzudat David reads it as acting like a grown man though still a boy. The Targum and Radak read it as a man who rules his own desires and fears sin.

sources.quote: עם שאתה עודך נער, התחזק עצמך להיות כאיש השלם בשניו
sources.says: Metzudat David says that though Solomon is still a boy, he must act like a man of full age.

sources.quote: לִגְבַר דָחֵיל חֶטְאִין
sources.says: The Targum translates 'a man who fears sin'.

sources.quote: זריז ומושל בנפשך וכובש את יצרך
sources.says: Radak says it means be quick, rule yourself, and conquer your urges.

2:3.headline: Will Solomon succeed, or act wisely?
2:3.body: תשכיל can mean 'you will succeed' or 'you will act with sense'. The Targum reads success. Malbim says success depends on luck, but acting wisely depends on good judgment.

sources.quote: תשכיל. כתרגומו תצלח
sources.says: Radak follows the Targum: 'you will succeed'.

sources.quote: שהצלחה תלויה במזל, וההשכלה תלויה בטוב שכל האדם
sources.says: Malbim separates success, which depends on luck, from acting wisely, which depends on a person's good sense.

2:5.headline: Blood of war spilled in peacetime
2:5.body: Joab 'put the blood of war in peace'. Radak reads it two ways. Joab killed men at peace as if at war. Or he avenged his brother, killed in battle, as if it had been murder in peacetime.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם שָׁלוֹם עִמּוֹ, וְלֹא הָיוּ נִשְׁמָרִים מִמֶּנּוּ
sources.says: Rashi says Abner and Amasa were at peace with Joab and did not guard themselves from him.

sources.quote: או פירוש וישם דמי מלחמה דמי עשאל שהיו דמי המלחמה
sources.says: Radak also reads it as Asahel's blood, shed in battle, which Joab treated as peacetime murder to avenge.

2:5.headline: What Joab's sandal had to do with two killings
2:5.body: The blood was 'on the sandal on his feet'. Ralbag says Joab bent to fix his sandal so his sword fell out near Amasa. A midrash in Rashi says he tricked Abner with a question about the rite of removing a shoe.

sources.quote: שחה לתקן נעלו אשר ברגליו ואז בשחותו נפל החרב מתערו לארץ
sources.says: Ralbag says Joab bent to fix his sandal, and the sword fell from its sheath, so Amasa did not guard against it.

sources.quote: שֶׁשְּׁאָלוֹ גִּדֶּמֶת הֵיאָךְ חוֹלֶצֶת
sources.says: Rashi says Joab killed Abner by a trick: he asked him how a woman without hands performs the shoe-removal rite.

2:8.headline: Shimei is 'with you': nearby, or your teacher?
2:8.body: David warns that Shimei is 'with you'. Plainly he lives near Solomon, in Jerusalem. The sages read it as Shimei being Solomon's Torah teacher.

sources.quote: ובדרש כי רבו היה והיה מלמדו וזהו טעם עמך
sources.says: Radak says 'with you' means in Jerusalem, within your power, and brings a midrash that Shimei was Solomon's teacher.

sources.quote: ורבותינו ז״ל אמרו שהיה מלמדו תורה
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it as a friend who sits with you, and cites the sages that he taught Solomon Torah.

2:19.headline: A throne for the king's mother, or for Ruth?
2:19.body: Plainly the chair is for Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. The sages read 'the mother of the king' as the mother of the royal line, Ruth. Radak calls this very far-fetched.

sources.quote: לְאִמָּהּ שֶׁל מַלְכוּת, הִיא רוּת
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: the mother of the kingship, that is Ruth.

sources.quote: והיא רות כי עדיין היתה היא בחייה וזה רחוק מאד
sources.says: Radak reports the midrash that Ruth was still alive and calls it very far-fetched.

2:28.headline: Joab 'did not side with Absalom': loyalty, or defiance?
2:28.body: The verse says Joab did not lean after Absalom. Rashi says he wanted to, but feared David's strength. Ralbag reads it against him: he did not spare Absalom as David had ordered.

sources.quote: אֲבָל בִּקֵּשׁ לִנְטוֹת, אֶלָּא נִתְיָרֵא שֶׁעֲדַיִן לַחְלוּחִית שֶׁל דָּוִד קַיֶּמֶת
sources.says: Rashi says Joab wanted to join Absalom but was afraid, because David still had his strength.

sources.quote: והשני כי לא נטה אחרי אבשלום להצילו מן המות כמו שצוהו דוד
sources.says: Ralbag says Joab felt guilty for not turning to save Absalom from death, as David had commanded.

2:28.headline: Joab grabbed the wrong part of the altar
2:28.body: Joab holds the horns of the altar to be safe. The sages said he erred: the altar shelters only on its top, not its horns, and only for an accidental killer.

sources.quote: שאין קולט רק גגו לא קרנותיו
sources.says: Malbim cites the sages that Joab made three mistakes, one being that the altar protects from its top and not from its horns.

sources.quote: כי בדבר זה טעה יואב כי לא היה קולט המזבח אלא על שגגה ועל גגו
sources.says: Radak says the altar protected only someone who killed by accident, and only on its top.

2:34.headline: Buried 'in his house in the wilderness': where, and why?
2:34.body: Plainly Joab had a house out in the grazing land. The sages read 'wilderness' as praise: his house was open to all, as a desert is open to everyone.

sources.quote: ויקרא גם כן מדבר מקום שהוא ביישוב אבל אינו עבוד
sources.says: Radak says מדבר can mean unfarmed land kept for grazing, where Joab had a house.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה בֵּיתוֹ הֶפְקֵר כַּמִּדְבָּר, לַעֲנִיִּים
sources.says: Rashi says his house was open to the poor, like a wilderness that belongs to no one.

2:42.headline: 'I testified against you' means 'I warned you'
2:42.body: ואעד comes from the word for witness. Rashi says here it means a formal warning, and Metzudat David explains that warnings were given before witnesses.

sources.quote: וָאָעִד בְּךָ. לְשׁוֹן הַתְרָאָה
sources.says: Rashi says the word means a warning.

sources.quote: ועל שם שדרך המתרה להתרות בעדים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the witness word is used because a warning is given in front of witnesses.

2:46.headline: First his rule was firm, now his whole kingdom
2:46.body: Verse 12 already said Solomon's rule was firm. Malbim says מלוכה is the king's own rule, but ממלכה is the country. Only now, with his enemies gone, was the country secure.

sources.quote: אבל נושא שם ממלכה הוא המדינה
sources.says: Malbim says מלוכה refers to the king and ממלכה to the realm, which still had opponents until now.

20:14.headline: 'Who will bind the battle?' means who will lead it
20:14.body: Ahab asks who will יאסר, literally 'bind', the battle. Radak says the leader of a battle is called a binder, because he starts and the people follow. Metzudat David says the leader binds his soldiers with orders.

sources.quote: כי ראש המלחמה יקרא אוסר לפי שהוא מתחיל והעם אחריו
sources.says: Radak says the head of a battle is called a binder because he begins and the people follow him.

sources.quote: וקושר אותם באזהרות בעניני המלחמה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the leader ties the soldiers to his orders about the battle.

20:18.headline: 'Alive' or 'lively': Ben-Hadad's order read two ways
20:18.body: Ben-Hadad orders his men to seize the Israelites חיים. Ralbag reads it plainly: take them alive, do not kill them. Metzudat David adds that חיים can mean quick and vigorous, as in 'son of a valiant man'.

sources.quote: יתפשום חיים ולא יהרגום
sources.says: Ralbag says either way they should take them alive and not kill them.

sources.quote: חיים הוא ענין זריזות, וכן (שמואל ב כג כ): בן איש חי
sources.says: Metzudat David says חיים can mean quickness, as in II Samuel 23:20.

20:22.headline: 'At the return of the year': when the sun comes back around
20:22.body: The prophet warns that Aram will attack again לתשובת השנה, at the year's 'return'. Rashi gives the Targum: at the end of the year. Radak says it is when the sun returns to the point where the year began.

sources.quote: לִזְמַן סוֹפָא דְּשַׁתָּא
sources.says: Rashi gives the Aramaic: at the time of the end of the year.

sources.quote: שתשוב השמש לנקודה אשר החלה ממנה בראש השנה
sources.says: Radak says it is when the sun returns to the point it started from at the year's start.

20:23.headline: Why Aram thought Israel's God ruled only the hills
20:23.body: Aram's officers say Israel's God is a god of הרים, hills. Ralbag notes that Samaria, where they lost, is built on a hill. Metzudat David suggests they thought so because the Torah was given on a mountain.

sources.quote: ידוע כי שמרון היה בנוי בהר
sources.says: Ralbag says Samaria was built on a hill.

sources.quote: על אשר נתן התורה לישראל על ההר
sources.says: Metzudat David suggests they thought this because the Torah was given to Israel on a mountain.

20:34.headline: The 'streets' in Damascus are markets whose fees go to Ahab
20:34.body: Ben-Hadad offers Ahab חצות in Damascus. Radak, with the Targum, says these are markets, and the customs from buying and selling there would be Ahab's. Metzudat David says Ahab could set up markets there as if it were his own city.

sources.quote: פירוש שוקים שיהיו מוצאי השוקים ממה שיקנו וימכרו בהם יהיה המכס שלו
sources.says: Radak says they are markets, and the customs from trade in them would belong to Ahab.

sources.quote: תעשה לך שווקים, כאילו היתה עירך
sources.says: Metzudat David says Ahab would make markets for himself as if Damascus were his city.

21:2.headline: A 'vegetable garden': Malbim suspects it was meant for idols
21:2.body: Ahab wants the vineyard for a garden of greens. Malbim says that meant tearing out vines, which is forbidden. He adds that Ahab used to set up Baal in his gardens.

sources.quote: באופן שרצה להשחית עצי הכרם (שהוא איסור) לזרוע בו ירק
sources.says: Malbim says Ahab wanted to destroy the vines, which is forbidden, to plant greens.

sources.quote: היה דרכו להעמיד הבעל על הגן שלו
sources.says: Malbim says Ahab's way was to set up Baal in his garden.

sources.quote: הוא העשב שהוא מאכל האדם או עשבים שיש להם ריח טוב
sources.says: Radak says ירק is plants people eat, or sweet-smelling herbs.

21:3.headline: 'Far be it from me by God': why bring God in?
21:3.body: Malbim asks why Naboth speaks as if selling were a grave sin. Metzudat David reads חלילה as 'profane': the Torah says land may not be sold for good.

sources.quote: למה אמר חלילה לי מה' כאלו יעשה בזה עון פלילי
sources.says: Malbim asks why Naboth said 'far be it from me by God', as if selling would be a serious crime.

sources.quote: חולין הוא לי, בעבור מצות ה׳, שאמרה התורה (ויקרא כה כג): והארץ לא תמכר לצמיתות
sources.says: Metzudat David says it would be profane for him, because the Torah says land must not be sold permanently.

21:3.headline: 'My fathers' inheritance': a jab at Ahab, who abandoned his
21:3.body: Naboth refuses to give up the land his fathers left him. Malbim says the words were also a rebuke. Ahab had given up his own fathers' inheritance, the God of his fathers.

sources.quote: רצה להוכיח בזה את אחאב שעזב נחלת אבותיו, שהוא ה' אלהי אבותיו
sources.says: Malbim says Naboth meant to rebuke Ahab, who abandoned his fathers' inheritance, the God of his fathers.

21:4.headline: Sullen and angry: what really stung Ahab
21:4.body: סר is a rare word for sullen, a spirit that has turned away. Malbim says Ahab was not upset about losing the vineyard. He was stung by Naboth's words, which rebuked him.

sources.quote: וז"ש שבא סר וזעף שהיה רוחו סרה מאתו, לא על גוף המעשה שלא השיג הכרם רק על הדבר אשר דבר אליו
sources.says: Malbim says סר means his spirit left him, not over failing to get the vineyard but over what Naboth said to him.

sources.quote: סר ממך הרצון והדבור
sources.says: Metzudat David says Jezebel means his will and speech had left him.

21:7.headline: 'Now you do kingship!' Jezebel's mocking question
21:7.body: The words can read as a plain statement. Radak and Metzudat David say it is a question in wonder: is this how a king behaves? A king should get his way, not sulk.

sources.quote: כתרגומו תצלח במלכותא והוא לשון תמיהה
sources.says: Radak says it means, as the Targum has it, 'will you succeed in kingship?', said in wonder.

sources.quote: אמרה בתמיה, וכי בדבר שאתה עושה עתה, תנהיג את המלוכה
sources.says: Metzudat David says she asked in wonder: is this how you run a kingdom?

21:9.headline: Call a fast, or call a gathering?
21:9.body: צום usually means a fast. Rashi and Radak say on a fast day people look into their sins, which suited Jezebel's plan. Radak's father read צום as 'gathering', from צומת, a meeting point.

sources.quote: וּבְיוֹם צוֹם דַּרְכָּם לִבְדֹּק בַּעֲבֵרוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדָם
sources.says: Rashi says on a fast day they would examine the sins among them.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פירש צום קבוץ וכן ביום צום שבירמיהו מלשון רז"ל צומת הגידין שהוא מקום קבוץ הגידין
sources.says: Radak says his father read צום as a gathering, from the Sages' word for the place where sinews meet.

21:10.headline: 'You blessed God and king' means you cursed them
