21:10.body: The charge says Naboth 'blessed' God and the king. Metzudat David says 'blessed' here is a polite stand-in for 'cursed'. The Targum says it plainly: he blasphemed God and cursed the king.

sources.quote: ברכת. הוא כנוי הקללה
sources.says: Metzudat David says 'blessed' is a substitute word for cursing.

sources.quote: ברכת אלהים ומלך. תרגומו גדיפתא קדם ה' ומלכא לטתא
sources.says: Radak gives the Targum: you blasphemed before God and cursed the king.

21:10.headline: Why accuse him of cursing God and the king?
21:10.body: One charge was enough for death. Radak says cursing the king was the point. A man the king executes forfeits his land to the king. A man the court executes leaves it to his heirs.

sources.quote: ומפני זה אמרה איזבל שיעידו העדים כי ברך נבות אלהים ומלך כי אילו יאמרו ברך אלהים לבד והיה דינו מסור לב"ד ויהיו נכסיו ליורשים
sources.says: Radak says Jezebel had both charges made because if he cursed only God, the court would judge him and his property would go to his heirs.

sources.quote: אמרה זה להגדיל קצף העם עליו ויסקלוהו מיד
sources.says: Radak also says she added both to stir the people's anger so they would stone him at once.

21:15.headline: 'Go inherit': how could Ahab inherit Naboth?
21:15.body: רש means 'inherit'. Rashi gives two views of the Sages. Either the king takes the land of a man he executes, or Ahab was Naboth's cousin and became heir after Naboth's sons were killed too.

sources.quote: יֵשׁ מֵחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: הֲרוּגֵי מַלְכוּת נִכְסֵיהֶם לַמֶּלֶךְ, וְיֵשׁ מֵהֶן אוֹמְרִים: בֶּן אֲחִי אָבִיו הָיָה, וְאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו הָרַג, וְרָאוּי לְיָרְשׁוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says some Sages hold the property of those the king executes goes to the king, and others say Naboth was Ahab's cousin, and with Naboth and his sons dead, Ahab was heir.

sources.quote: אמר לשון ירושה לפי שנפלו לו נכסיו בדין והוא במקום היורשים
sources.says: Radak says the word 'inherit' is used because the property fell to Ahab by law, in place of the heirs.

21:15.headline: 'Not alive, but dead': why say it twice?
21:15.body: Jezebel says Naboth is not alive, then adds that he is dead. Radak says the extra word means he died by royal sentence, not a natural death. So his land belongs to the king.

sources.quote: אחר שאמר כי אין נבות חי למה אמר כי מת לומר שלא מת מיתת עצמו אלא מת שנתחייב מיתה למלך ונכסיו למלך
sources.says: Radak asks why she adds 'he is dead' after 'he is not alive', and says it means he did not die naturally but was sentenced by the king, so his property is the king's.

21:19.headline: 'In the place' Naboth died, or in the same way?
21:19.body: Later the dogs lick Ahab's blood at the pool of Samaria, not in Jezreel. Ralbag says 'in the place' may mean in the same manner. Or it means the same place, but the punishment was delayed because Ahab repented.

sources.quote: אין הרצון בזה שילקקו הכלבים את דם אחאב במקום שנסקל נבות כי על ברכת שמרון לקקו הכלבים דם אחאב
sources.says: Ralbag says it does not mean the dogs licked Ahab's blood where Naboth was stoned, since they licked it at the pool of Samaria.

sources.quote: ואפשר שנאמ' שהרצון בו כי במקום ההוא בעינו ילוקו הכלבי' את דמו אך מפני כי נכנע אחאב מפני השם ית' האריך לו זה עד ימי בנו
sources.says: Ralbag says it may mean that very place, but because Ahab humbled himself, God put it off to his son's days.

21:20.headline: 'Have you found me?' Ahab tries to shift the blame
21:20.body: Ahab asks if Elijah has 'found' him guilty. Malbim says Ahab meant that Jezebel did the killing, not him. Elijah answers 'I have found': Ahab sold himself to do her will.

sources.quote: המצאתני ר"ל וכי מצאת אותי בזה וכי אני רצחתיו והלא נהרג שלא על ידי רק ע"י איזבל
sources.says: Malbim says Ahab meant: have you found me guilty here? Did I murder him? He was killed by Jezebel, not me.

sources.quote: וחשב לכחש בפני הנביא, כאילו לא נעשתה מדעתו
sources.says: Metzudat David says Ahab thought to deny it to the prophet, as if it was done without his knowledge.

21:20.headline: Ahab 'sold himself' to do evil
21:20.body: Radak says Ahab acted as if he had sold himself to evil. Malbim says he sold himself to Jezebel, so her deeds count as his. Radak also cites a midrash that Ahab erased God's name from Scripture and wrote Baal instead.

sources.quote: כאילו מכר עצמו לעשות רע וכל עניניו וכל עסקיו לרע
sources.says: Radak says it is as if he sold himself to do evil, with all his affairs turned to evil.

sources.quote: וכאילו אתה נמכר לאיזבל אשתך לענין עשות הרע
sources.says: Malbim says it is as though Ahab were sold to Jezebel his wife to do evil.

sources.quote: מוחק האזכרות וכותב תחתיהם שם הבעל
sources.says: Radak cites a midrash that Ahab erased the names of God and wrote Baal in their place.

21:21.headline: 'One who pisses against a wall': every male, or even the dogs
21:21.body: This rare, crude phrase means wiping out Ahab's house. Metzudat David says it means every male. Radak says it is an exaggeration: not even a dog will be left. The Targum renders it 'anyone with sense'.

sources.quote: משתין בקיר. זה הזכר
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means the male.

sources.quote: דרך גוזמא אפילו הכלב לא ישאיר לו וי"ת ידע מדע
sources.says: Radak says it is an exaggeration, not even a dog will be left him, and the Targum renders it 'one who knows'.

21:23.headline: Jezebel eaten 'by the wall', in the valley, or on the plot?
21:23.body: חל is a rare word. Metzudat Zion says it is a low wall. Rashi says it is the valley of Jezreel. Radak notes the Targum reads it as חלק, the 'plot' of Jezreel, as if a letter were missing.

sources.quote: בחל. היא חומה נמוכה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חל is a low wall.

sources.quote: בְּבִקְעַת יִזְרְעֶאל, בְּחֵל, תַּרְגּוּמוֹ שֶׁל גַּיְא
sources.says: Rashi says it means the valley of Jezreel, since חל is the Aramaic for valley.

sources.quote: ולדעתו חסר קו"ף והוא כמו בחלק יזרעאל
sources.says: Radak says the Targum read it as missing a qof, like 'in the plot of Jezreel'.

21:27.headline: Ahab walked 'softly': slowly, barefoot, or in hiding?
21:27.body: אט is a rare word. Metzudat David and Radak say Ahab walked slowly, like a mourner. Rashi follows the Targum: barefoot. Ralbag adds he may have walked in secret, so no one would see.

sources.quote: הלך בנחת הנה והנה, כדרך אדם הדואג ומתאבל
sources.says: Metzudat David says he walked slowly back and forth, like a worried mourner.

sources.quote: וַיְהַלֵּךְ אַט. יָחֵף
sources.says: Rashi says it means barefoot.

sources.quote: או ירצה באמרו ויהלך אט שכבר הלך בסתר
sources.says: Ralbag says it may mean he walked secretly.

21:29.headline: Humbled before God's greatness, or from fear of punishment?
21:29.body: The verse uses two forms, מלפני and מפני. Malbim says the first means awe of God's greatness, the second fear of punishment. Ahab had only fear, so the evil was put off, not cancelled. Metzudat David reads it the other way: Ahab was humbled by God's greatness.

sources.quote: יש הבדל בין מלפני ובין מפני, שמלפני הוא מפני גדלו ורוממתו ומפני הוא מפני יראת העונש
sources.says: Malbim says מלפני means before God's greatness and מפני means from fear of punishment.

sources.quote: לא מפחד העונש, כי אם מגדולת האדון ה׳
sources.says: Metzudat David says Ahab was humbled not from fear of punishment but from God's greatness.

22:3.headline: Are they being lazy, or keeping quiet?
22:3.body: Ahab says 'we are מחשים' about taking back Ramoth-gilead. Rashi reads it as being lazy about it. Metzudat Zion reads it as keeping silent, as in 'a time to keep silent'.

sources.quote: וַאֲנַחְנוּ מַחְשִׁים. מִתְעַצְּלִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means we are being slow and lazy.

sources.quote: שותקים, כמו (קהלת ג ז) עת לחשות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means we are silent, as in 'a time to keep silent'.

22:7.headline: 'Is there not another prophet of the LORD?' Where does 'another' belong?
22:7.body: Read one way, Jehoshaphat calls the 400 prophets of the LORD and asks for one more. Ralbag says עוד belongs with 'is there not here a prophet', so he is hinting that none of the 400 is the LORD's.

sources.quote: והנה מלת עוד שבה אל אמרו האין פה נביא לא אל אמרו האין פה נביא לה'
sources.says: Ralbag says the word עוד goes with 'is there no prophet here', not with 'prophet of the LORD'.

22:10.headline: Why say the kings were 'dressed in clothes'?
22:10.body: Radak asks why the verse says the kings wore clothes, since of course they were not naked. He says בגדים here means fine royal robes.

sources.quote: פירוש בגדים חמודות כי מה שהיה אומר מלובשים ידענו כי לא היו ערומים אלא פי' בגדי מלכות חמודות
sources.says: Radak says it means fine clothes: we know they were not naked, so it must mean royal robes.

22:10.headline: At a threshing floor, or seated in a half circle like one?
22:10.body: The kings sit בגרן, at a threshing floor, by the city gate. Radak gives the plain reading. He also quotes the rabbis, who say it means they sat in a half circle shaped like a threshing floor, as the Sanhedrin did.

sources.quote: וכי שער שמרון גורן היה אלא לאו כגורן דתניא סנהדרין היתה כחצי גורן עגולה
sources.says: Radak cites the rabbis: the gate of Samaria was not a threshing floor, so it means they sat like one, in a half circle like the Sanhedrin.

22:15.headline: Micaiah's 'Go up and succeed' is mockery, not prophecy
22:15.body: Micaiah first repeats the false prophets' words. Radak says he said it mockingly and did not say 'Thus says the LORD'. Metzudat David says it was either mockery or a plain blessing.

sources.quote: דרך התול אמר לו כלשון שאר הנביאים ולא אמר לו כה אמר ה'
sources.says: Radak says he said it in mockery, in the words of the other prophets, and not in God's name.

sources.quote: מעצמו אמר לו בברכה, הלואי שתצליח וימסרם ה׳ בידך או, שאמר בלעג והתול
sources.says: Metzudat David says he either spoke on his own as a blessing, or said it in scorn.

22:19.headline: 'I saw the LORD': seeing with the mind, not the eyes
22:19.body: Micaiah says he saw God on His throne. Maimonides says that when the Bible speaks of seeing God, it means understanding with the mind. Here it was a prophetic vision.

sources.quote: כל אלה השגה שכלית, לא ראיית עין כלל
sources.says: Maimonides lists this verse among those where seeing God means grasping with the mind, not seeing with the eye.

sources.quote: וכדברי מיכיהו בן ימלא
sources.says: Maimonides cites Micaiah's words as an example of a prophetic dream in which God seems to speak.

22:19.headline: Angels on God's left: those who argue for guilt
22:19.body: The heavenly host stands to God's right and left. Rashi asks how there can be a 'left' above. He says those on the right argue for merit and those on the left argue for guilt.

sources.quote: וְכִי יֵשׁ שְׂמֹאל לְמַעְלָה
sources.says: Rashi asks whether there is a left side above.

sources.quote: אלא אלו מימינים לזכות ואלו משמאילים לחובה
sources.says: Radak cites the rabbis: some lean toward merit and some toward guilt.

22:20.headline: Who will lure Ahab? Radak says the scene is not literal
22:20.body: God asks who will lure Ahab to his death. Radak says this is very puzzling if taken literally. He reads it as God stirring the false prophets' own wish to tell Ahab what he wanted to hear.

sources.quote: הדברים האלה הם מבוכה גדולה למי שמבין אותם כמשמעו והאמת כי האל העיר רוח נביאי שקר לפתות את אחאב
sources.says: Radak says these words are deeply confusing if read literally, and the truth is that God stirred the false prophets to lure Ahab.

22:21.headline: 'The spirit' that came forward: the rabbis say it was Naboth's
22:21.body: The verse says 'the spirit' with no name. Rashi and Radak, following the rabbis, say it was the spirit of Naboth, whom Ahab had killed. He came to bring about Ahab's fall.

sources.quote: וַיֵּצֵא הָרוּחַ. רוּחוֹ שֶׁל נָבוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it was the spirit of Naboth.

sources.quote: והרוח רוח נבות
sources.says: Radak, citing Maimonides, says the spirit was Naboth's.

22:30.headline: 'Disguise yourself'? No, Ahab means 'I will disguise myself'
22:30.body: It looks like Ahab tells Jehoshaphat to disguise himself, then tells him to wear his own robes. Rashi and Ralbag read התחפש as a plain verb form, not an order: Ahab is saying he will disguise himself.

sources.quote: לְהִתְחַפֵּשׂ וְלָבֹא, אֲנִי אֶתְחַפֵּשׂ
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'to disguise and go': I will disguise myself.

sources.quote: הנה התחפש הוא מקור
sources.says: Ralbag says התחפש is an infinitive, not a command.

22:32.headline: Jehoshaphat cried out: to God, or to his soldiers?
22:32.body: Rashi says Jehoshaphat cried out to God. Metzudat David says he called his own men to come and help him.

sources.quote: וַיִּזְעַק יְהוֹשָׁפָט. לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says he cried out to God.

sources.quote: ויזעק. לאנשיו לבוא לעזרו
sources.says: Metzudat David says he called to his men to come help him.

22:34.headline: A random arrow, and the end of two prophecies
22:34.body: לתמו means the archer shot without aiming at the king. Radak quotes a midrash that hears תמו, 'they were completed': the two prophecies of Elijah and Micaiah about Ahab's death came true.

sources.quote: ובדרש לתמו תמו שני חזיונות של אליהו ושל מיכיהו
sources.says: Radak quotes a midrash: 'לתמו' means the two visions of Elijah and Micaiah were completed.

sources.quote: לֹא יָדַע שֶׁהוּא מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says the archer did not know it was the king of Israel.

22:34.headline: Ahab says 'I am sick', not 'I am wounded'
22:34.body: Ahab was hit by an arrow but tells his driver only that he is sick. Radak and Ralbag say he hid the wound so his army would not lose heart.

sources.quote: כי גם לרכבו לא רצה לגלות שהוכה אלא אמר לו כי החלה לא שהוכה
sources.says: Radak cites his father: Ahab did not want even his driver to know he was hit, so he said he was ill.

sources.quote: לא רצה להגיד כי הוכה כדי שלא ירך לב ישראל
sources.says: Ralbag says he did not want to say he was hit, so Israel would not lose heart.

22:36.headline: A herald's cry through the camp, or a cheer at Ahab's death?
22:36.body: רנה usually means a ringing shout of joy. The Targum, Ralbag and Radak read it here as a herald's call. Radak also quotes a midrash that reads it as joy: 'when the wicked perish there is singing'.

sources.quote: הרצון בו ויעבר קול הרנה והיא הצעקה וענינו קול הכרוז
sources.says: Ralbag says it means a cry, the voice of a herald.

sources.quote: ובדרש ויעבור הרנה באבוד רשעים רנה
sources.says: Radak quotes a midrash that links it to 'when the wicked perish there is joyful song'.

22:38.headline: Harlots, or weapons? And a midrash hears 'visions'
22:38.body: The plain text says harlots bathed in the pool. The Targum reads it as weapons washed there. Radak also quotes a midrash that hears חזיונות, visions: the prophecies of Elijah and Micaiah came true.

sources.quote: וּכְלֵי הַזַּיִן רָחֲצּוּ שָׁם מִן הַדָּם, כָּךְ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן
sources.says: Rashi says the Targum reads it as weapons washed of the blood there.

sources.quote: ועוד דרשו הזונות כמו חזיונות הגיעו שני חזיונות של אליהו ושל מיכה
sources.says: Radak quotes a midrash that reads הזונות as visions: the two visions of Elijah and Micaiah were fulfilled.

22:49.headline: Written 'ten', read 'made': Jehoshaphat made ten ships
22:49.body: The written text has עשר, ten, but it is read עשה, made. Radak and Ralbag say both are meant: he made ten ships.

sources.quote: כן כתוב וקרי עשה והכתוב אומר כי עשר ספינות הם שעשה
sources.says: Radak says the written form teaches that he made ten ships.

sources.quote: ידמה שעשר אניות עשה ולזה כתו' עשר וקרי עשה
sources.says: Ralbag says it seems he made ten ships, which is why it is written 'ten' and read 'made'.

4:3.headline: The "reminder": keeper of records, or keeper of the court's order
4:3.body: המזכיר comes from the word for remembering. Metzudat David and the Targum say he kept the royal records. Rashi reports another reading: he reminded the king which case came first, so it would be judged first.

sources.quote: אֵיזֶה מִשְׁפָּט בָּא לְפָנָיו רִאשׁוֹן, שֶׁיִּפְסְקֶנּוּ רִאשׁוֹן, כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי
sources.says: Rashi says, as he heard it, the recorder noted which case came before the king first, so the king would decide it first.

sources.quote: ממונה על ספר הזכרונות
sources.says: Metzudat David says he was in charge of the book of records.

sources.quote: יְהוֹשָׁפָט בַּר אֲחִילוּד מְמַנָא עַל דָכְרָנַיָא
sources.says: The Targum calls Jehoshaphat the officer over the records.

4:4.headline: Abiathar is listed as priest, though Solomon had banished him
4:4.body: In chapter 2 Solomon removed Abiathar as priest and sent him home to Anathoth. Radak suggests this is a different priest with the same name. Ralbag says Abiathar still had to serve when Zadok was not fit to.

sources.quote: כי הנה שלמה גרשהו מהיות כהן גדול ואמר לו ענתות לך אל שדיך אלא מן הדומה כי כהן אחר היה שמו אביתר
sources.says: Radak says it is strange, since Solomon banished Abiathar, so it seems likely another priest was named Abiathar.

sources.quote: הנה הוכרח לעבוד בעת היות צדוק בלתי ראוי לעבוד
sources.says: Ralbag says that although Abiathar was banished, he had to serve at times when Zadok was not fit to serve.

4:5.headline: The king's רעה: his best man, always at his side
4:5.body: רעה is a rare word for companion. The Targum calls Zabud the king's שושבין, the word for a groom's best man. Radak and Metzudat David say he was with the king all the time.

sources.quote: שושבינא דמלכא שהיה עמו תמיד
sources.says: Radak gives the Targum's "the king's best man" and says he was always with the king.

sources.quote: ישב עמו בתמידות, להשתעשע עמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says he sat with the king constantly, to keep him company.

4:13.headline: A region called a "rope", for the rope that measured land
4:13.body: חבל usually means rope. Here it means a region. Metzudat Zion says a district is called חבל because land shares were measured out with a rope.

sources.quote: המחוז תקרא חבל, כי בחבל תחלק נחלה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a district is called a חבל because an inheritance is divided with a rope.

4:19.headline: One more officer: a chief over all, or one for the leap month
4:19.body: The list has twelve officers, one for each month, then adds "one officer in the land". Rashi gives two views: an officer over the other twelve, or an extra one for the added month of a leap year.

sources.quote: חַד אָמַר: אֶחָד מְמֻנֶּה עַל כֻּלָּם, הוּא עֲזַרְיָה בֶּן נָתָן הָאָמוּר לְמַעְלָה, וְחַד אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד חֹדֶשׁ הָעִבּוּר
sources.says: Rashi says Rav and Shmuel disagree: one says it is an officer over all of them, Azariah son of Nathan, and one says it is for the leap month.

sources.quote: או היה שם נציב אחד לחדש העבור והביאור הראשון יותר נכון
sources.says: Ralbag gives both readings and says the first, an officer over the others, is more correct.

5:8.headline: Rekhesh: a fast horse, or a mule?
5:8.body: The commentators agree רכש is some kind of animal kept beside the horses. Ralbag thinks it is the fastest kind of horse, used in war. Radak also brings a view that it means mules.

sources.quote: וי"א שהם פרדים בני הסוסיות
sources.says: Radak says it is a kind of animal, and some say it means mules born of mares.

sources.quote: ואחשוב שהם היותר קלי המרוץ והם אשר ירכבו בהם במלחמה
sources.says: Ralbag thinks the רכש is a kind of horse, the fastest ones, ridden in battle.

5:11.headline: The sages hear Joseph the provider in the name Kalkol
5:11.body: A midrash reads the four wise men as hidden names for great figures. Kalkol sounds like ויכלכל, 'he provided', said of Joseph feeding his family.

sources.quote: וכלכל זה יוסף שנאמר ויכלכל יוסף
sources.says: Radak brings the sages' teaching that Kalkol means Joseph, because the Torah says Joseph provided for his family.

sources.quote: וְכַלְכֹּל — זֶה יוֹסֵף
sources.says: Rashi brings the same midrash that Kalkol is Joseph.

5:11.headline: Darda read as 'the generation of knowledge'
5:11.body: In the midrash, Darda is the generation that left Egypt. Radak explains the name as דור דעה, a generation that had knowledge.

sources.quote: דרדע זה דור המדבר דור שיש בהם דעה
sources.says: Radak brings the sages' reading that Darda is the generation of the desert, a generation with knowledge.

sources.quote: וְדַרְדַּע — זֶה דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר
sources.says: Rashi brings the midrash that Darda is the desert generation.

5:13.headline: The Targum turns Solomon's talk of trees into prophecy
5:13.body: The verse says Solomon spoke about trees. Targum Jonathan renders it as prophecy about the kings of David's line, as if the trees stood for them.

sources.quote: וְאִתְנַבֵּי עַל מַלְכֵי בֵית דָוִד
sources.says: The Targum says he prophesied about the kings of the house of David who would rule.

sources.quote: וי"ת פסוק וידבר על העצים כן ואתנבי על מלכי בית דוד
sources.says: Radak points out that the Targum translates 'he spoke about the trees' as prophecy about David's kings.

5:13.headline: Cedar and hyssop: the tallest plant and the lowest
5:13.body: The sages connect this pair to the cleansing of a person struck with tzaraat, which uses cedar and hyssop. Radak says pride like a tall cedar brought the disease, and lowering oneself like hyssop heals it.

sources.quote: ע"י שהגביה עצמו כארז לקה בצרעת כיון שמשפיל עצמו כאזוב נטהר ונתרפא
sources.says: Radak says the person raised himself like a cedar and was struck, and once he lowers himself like hyssop he is cleansed.

sources.quote: הוא הגדול וקטן במיני הצמחים והעד מדברי חכמת שלמה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says cedar and hyssop are the largest and smallest plants, and brings this verse as proof.

5:32.headline: Men of Gebal, or stone-cutters who set borders
5:32.body: Rashi reads הגבלים as people from the city of Gebal, known as builders. Radak also brings a reading from גבול, a border, because they cut each stone to its exact edge.

sources.quote: אֻמָּה שֶׁשְּׁמָהּ גְּבָל, וּבְקִיאִים לְסַתֵּת אֲבָנִים
sources.says: Rashi says they were a nation called Gebal, skilled at cutting stones and building.

sources.quote: והוא מענין גבול שנותנין גבול לאבן בפסלם אותה
sources.says: Radak says the word may come from גבול, since they set a border for each stone as they cut it, and also brings the Gebal reading.

7:19.headline: The lily is named for its six petals
7:19.body: The pillar tops were shaped like a שושן, a lily. Metzudat Zion says the flower got its name because it always has six (שש) leaves.

sources.quote: ועל שהוא תמיד בת ששת עלין, קרויה שושן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the plant is called שושן because it always has six leaves.

7:21.headline: The pillar Yachin: may the house stand firm forever
7:21.body: Solomon named the right pillar יכין, from a word meaning "set firm". Radak says the pillars at the entrance got names as a good sign that the house would stand forever.

sources.quote: לאחד יכין לשון הכנה שיכון הבית לעולם כמו שאמר כירח יכון עולם
sources.says: Radak says יכין comes from setting firm, a wish that the house would stand forever.

7:21.headline: The pillar Boaz: "in it is strength"
7:21.body: Radak reads בעז as two words joined, בו עז, "in it is strength". The name was a wish that God would give the house strength and long life.

sources.quote: ובועז לשון עוז והיא מלה מורכבת בו עז כלומר שיתן האל בו עוז וקיום
sources.says: Radak says בועז is a joined word, בו עז, meaning God would put strength and endurance in the house.

7:33.headline: Solomon's wheels copied the chariot Ezekiel saw
7:33.body: The stands had wheels "like a chariot wheel". Radak says this means God's chariot in Ezekiel's vision: Solomon saw by wisdom what Ezekiel later saw in prophecy.

sources.quote: וראה שלמה בחכמתו מה שראה יחזקאל בנבואתו
sources.says: Radak says Solomon saw through his wisdom what Ezekiel saw in his prophecy.

sources.quote: אופן בתוך האופן שתי וערב, כמו שאמר ביחזקאל
sources.says: Rashi says these were wheels set inside wheels, crosswise, as Ezekiel describes the chariot.

7:40.headline: These כירות are ash pots, not wash basins
7:40.body: Earlier in the chapter כיור means a basin for washing. Here Rashi and Metzudat Zion say the word means pots, the same as סירות, used to clear ashes from the altar.

sources.quote: ואמר רבי, הכירות הן הן סירות
sources.says: Rashi says the כירות here are the same as סירות, pots.

sources.quote: הכירות. של נחשת, לדשן את המזבח
sources.says: Rashi says these were bronze pots for clearing the altar's ashes.

sources.quote: הכירות. הסירות, כמו (שמואל א ב יד) והכה בכיור
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means pots, as in I Samuel 2:14.

7:45.headline: Written "the tent", read aloud as "these"
7:45.body: The word is read האלה, "these", but written האהל, "the tent". Radak says the written form hints that Hiram made the vessels like those of Moses' Tent of Meeting.

sources.quote: והכתיב ר"ל כעין אותם הכלים שהיו באהל מועד כן עשה חירם
sources.says: Radak says the written form means Hiram made the vessels like the ones in the Tent of Meeting.

7:47.headline: Solomon stopped weighing, or set the vessels in place?
7:47.body: Rashi reads וינח as "left off": there was so much bronze that Solomon stopped weighing it. The Targum, as Radak reports, reads it as "set down": he put the vessels in their places in the Temple.

sources.quote: מלשקל את משקל הכלים האלה מרב מאד וחדל לספר משקלם
sources.says: Rashi says Solomon left off weighing the vessels because there were so many, and stopped counting their weight.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם ואצנע שלמה כלומר הביאם ממקום יציקתם והניחם בבית המקדש במקומם
sources.says: Radak says the Targum reads it as Solomon bringing the vessels from where they were cast and setting them in their places in the Temple.

7:50.headline: Musical instruments, or jugs?
7:50.body: Rashi says ספות and מזמרות are both kinds of musical instruments. Metzudat Zion, following the Targum, says ספות are jugs.

sources.quote: כלי של מיני זמר הוא, וכן מזמרות
sources.says: Rashi says ספות is a kind of musical instrument, and so are מזמרות.

sources.quote: כלים כעין כדים, כי תרגם יונתן: קולין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they were vessels like jugs, as the Targum translates.

7:51.headline: Why Solomon would not build with David's gifts
7:51.body: Rashi brings a midrash that Solomon stored what David had set aside instead of building with it. One reason: the money should have fed the poor during the three-year famine in David's time.

sources.quote: ומדרש אגדה: שלא רצה שלמה לתת מאותו הקדש לבנין הבית
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash that Solomon did not want to use David's gifts to build the Temple.

sources.quote: רעב היה בימי אביו שלש שנים, שנה אחר שנה, והיה לו לבזבז ההקדשות הללו, להחיות בהן עניי ישראל
sources.says: Rashi gives one reason: there was a three-year famine in David's day, and he should have spent these gifts to keep Israel's poor alive.

8:2.headline: The month of Etanim: "the strong ones", or "the ancient month"?
8:2.body: Etanim is an old name for the seventh month. Radak says איתן means strength: the crops that keep people alive are gathered then. He also reports the Sages' readings and the Targum's "ancient month", once counted first.

sources.quote: וכן איתנים לשון חוזק שהתבואות והפירות חיי האדם
sources.says: Radak says איתנים means strength, since the grain and fruit gathered in that month are people's life.

sources.quote: ומרבו' ז"ל שאמרו חדש שנולדו בו אבות הם איתני עולם
sources.says: Radak reports that some Sages said it is the month the patriarchs, "the strong ones of the world", were born.

sources.quote: בירחא דעתיקיא דקרן לה ירחא קדמאה
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum: the ancient month, which was once called the first month.

8:5.headline: Summoned versus gathered: two words for coming together
8:5.body: Malbim says נועד means people invited for a set time, so it fits the elders Solomon called. The rest of Israel are said to have gathered, because they came on their own.

sources.quote: שיעד לא נאמר רק על מי שהזמינו אותו לבוא לזמן מועד ומוגבל, וכל ישראל לא נועדו רק נקהלו מעצמם
sources.says: Malbim says יעד is used only of someone invited to come at a fixed time, while all Israel were not summoned but gathered by themselves.

8:8.headline: The poles were seen, yet not seen outside
8:8.body: The verse says the poles of the Ark could be seen, and also that they could not be seen outside. Rashi says they pushed against the curtain and bulged through it, without tearing it.

sources.quote: יכול יהיו מקרעין בה ויוצאין, תלמוד לומר ולא יראו החוצה, הא כיצד, דוחקין ובולטין
sources.says: Rashi says one might think the poles tore through the curtain, but "not seen outside" teaches that they pressed against it and bulged out.

8:9.headline: "Nothing but the two tablets": or something more inside?
8:9.body: Radak takes the verse at its word: only the two tablets were in the Ark. Malbim explains why the Sages read more into it. Hebrew rarely puts רק after "there is not", and two limits in a row add something.

sources.quote: זה ראייה כי לא היו בארון לא שברי לוחות ולא ס"ת
sources.says: Radak says this proves there were no broken tablets and no Torah scroll in the Ark.

sources.quote: אין בארון רק הוה מיעוט אחר מיעוט ואין מיעוט אחר מיעוט אלא לרבות
sources.says: Malbim explains the Sages' reading: "there is not" followed by "only" is one limit after another, and that adds something.

8:15.headline: God's word, fulfilled "by His hand" through a person's choice
8:15.body: Rashi reads "by His hand" as God keeping His word. Malbim adds that God's word works at once, except where a person is free to choose. There God fills it "by hand", by moving Solomon's heart to build.

sources.quote: קים את דברו בידו הטובה
sources.says: Rashi says God kept His word with His good hand.

sources.quote: אין הדבור פועל עד שממלא הדבר בידו ר"ל שמניע את האדם ומטה חפצו ובחירתו לעשות כדבר ה'
sources.says: Malbim says that where a person has free choice, God's word does not act until He fills it by hand, moving the person's will to do it.

8:27.headline: כלכל usually means "feed"; here it means "contain"
8:27.body: The verb כלכל often means to provide for someone. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say that here it means to hold or contain: even the heavens cannot hold God.

sources.quote: לא יכלכלוך.} לא יכילוך
sources.says: Rashi says it means "cannot contain you".

sources.quote: ענין החזקה, כמו (לעיל ז כו) אלפים בת יכיל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means holding, as when the bronze sea held two thousand measures.

8:30.headline: Three words for prayer: praise, pouring out, and asking
8:30.body: Solomon uses three words for prayer. Malbim says רנה is praise and תפלה is pouring out the soul. תחנה is asking for needs, related to חנם, a free gift asked even by one who has not earned it.

sources.quote: הוא ספור שבחי המקום כמ"ש חז"ל לעולם יזכיר אדם שבחו של מקום
sources.says: Malbim says רנה is telling God's praise, as the Sages say one should praise God before praying.

sources.quote: עקרה שפיכת הנפש ודבקות הרוח
sources.says: Malbim says תפלה is at heart the pouring out of the soul and the spirit's clinging to God.

sources.quote: היא בקשת הצרכים, וענינה מענין חנון ומתנת חנם
sources.says: Malbim says תחנה is asking for one's needs, from the words for gracious and for a free gift.

8:31.headline: נשא here is not "lift" but "lend": the oath as a debt
8:31.body: נשא usually means to lift or carry. Rashi, Radak and Metzudat Zion read it here as a creditor's word. The oath is laid on the man like a debt.

sources.quote: ונשא בו.} לשון נושה
sources.says: Rashi says ונשא בו comes from the word for a creditor.

sources.quote: נשא מענין משאת מאומה שהוא לשון חוב
sources.says: Radak says נשא comes from the word for a loan, meaning a debt.

sources.quote: ונשא.} ענין חוב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means debt.

8:38.headline: "The plague of his heart": his sin, or his private pain?
8:38.body: Metzudat Zion reads נגע לבבו as a person's sin. Radak reads it as the trouble each person knows in his own heart, which others may not see.

sources.quote: נגע לבבו.} רצה לומר: עון וחטא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says "the plague of his heart" means sin and wrongdoing.

sources.quote: כל איש ואיש לפי נגעו אשר ידעו לבו ממה שלא נודע לאחרים
sources.says: Radak says it means each person's own trouble, which his heart knows and others do not.

8:43.headline: Why the foreigner gets everything he asks for
8:43.body: For Israel, Solomon asks God to give each person what his ways deserve. For the foreigner he asks for everything. Rashi says an Israelite whose prayer fails blames his own sins, but a foreigner would say the Temple is worthless.

sources.quote: לפי שישראל מכיר בהקב"ה, ויודע שהיכלת בידו, ואם אין תפלתו נשמעת, תולה את הדבר בעצמו ובחטאו
sources.says: Rashi says an Israelite knows God's power, so if his prayer is not answered he blames himself and his sin.

sources.quote: אבל עובד גלולים קורא תגר
sources.says: Rashi says an idol worshipper would complain that the famous house has nothing to it.

8:51.headline: An "iron furnace" though furnaces were made of clay
8:51.body: A כור is a furnace for refining gold and silver. Radak notes that such furnaces were made of earth, not iron. The word "iron" stresses how hard Israel was refined in Egypt.

sources.quote: והכורים לא יעשו אותם מברזל אלא מאדמה אמר הברזל לחזוק הצרוף שנצרפו שם
sources.says: Radak says furnaces are made of earth, not iron, and "iron" is said to show how strongly they were refined there.

8:59.headline: משפט here may mean daily needs, not judgment
8:59.body: משפט usually means justice. Rashi reads it here as God taking up His people's cause against enemies. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as their needs, given day by day.

sources.quote: לתבע עלבונם מיד האויב
sources.says: Rashi says it means to demand payment from the enemy for the wrongs done to them.

sources.quote: משפט.} ענין צורך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says משפט here means need.

sources.quote: לתת לנו דבר יום ביומו מה שאנו צריכים
sources.says: Radak says it means giving us each day what we need.

9:1.headline: חשק: what Solomon built just because he wanted to
9:1.body: חשק is a rare word for desire. Malbim says the Temple and the palace were needed, but beyond them Solomon built things he did not need, out of the wish to build.

sources.quote: חשק. ענין תאוה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חשק means desire.

sources.quote: וזולת זה בנה בנינים שלא היה צריך להם רק שחפץ לעשות לבנות ולנטוע ולהגדיל מעשיו
sources.says: Malbim says that besides the needed buildings, Solomon built ones he did not need, because he wanted to build, plant and make his works great.

9:2.headline: "A second time", though God had spoken to him twice before
9:2.body: God spoke to Solomon at Gibeon, and again while the Temple was being built. Malbim says the message during the building does not count, because it was a lower level of prophecy.

sources.quote: והגם שהיתה זאת הפעם השלישית, המראה שראה בתחילת הבנין אינה מן החשבון שלא היתה נבואה גמורה
sources.says: Malbim says that although this was the third time, the vision at the start of the building is not counted, since it was not full prophecy.

9:3.headline: God's "heart" here means His will
9:3.body: Maimonides says לב can mean will, and is used that way of God. Radak reads "My eyes and My heart" as My care and My will. Rashi gives the Targum: My heart is there if My will is done there.

sources.quote: הוא שמו של הרצון
sources.says: Maimonides says one meaning of לב is will.

sources.quote: יש שהוא מושאל לה' במשמעות זו
sources.says: Maimonides says the word is sometimes applied to God in this sense, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: השגחתי ורצוני יהי שם כל הימים
sources.says: Radak says it means My care and My will will be there always.

sources.quote: אִם לִבִּי וְחֶפְצִי שָׁם
sources.says: Rashi, following the Targum, ties God's presence to whether His heart and desire are done there.

9:7.headline: שנינה: Israel becomes a story the nations repeat
9:7.body: שנינה is a rare word. Rashi and Metzudat Zion link it to ושננתם, "repeat them", from the Shema. The nations will retell Israel's troubles and mock.

sources.quote: יְסַפְּרוּ אֶת הָרָעוֹת הַבָּאוֹת עָלָיו וְיִתְלַעֲגוּ בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says they will tell of the troubles that come on Israel and mock it.

sources.quote: וּלְשׁוֹן 'שְׁנִינָה' אַף הוּא לְשׁוֹן 'דִּבּוּר', דִּכְתִיב: וְשִׁנַּנְתָּם לְבָנֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says שנינה is a word for speech, as in "repeat them to your children".

sources.quote: ענין דבור, כמו (דברים ו ז) ושננתם לבניך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means speech, like ושננתם in Deuteronomy 6:7.

9:8.headline: "This house will be high": once lofty, or cut down?
9:8.body: The verse is a warning, yet it says the house "will be עליון", high. Rashi, Metzudat David and the Targum read it as: the house that was high will lie in ruins. Radak also reports a reading of עליון as "cut off".

sources.quote: וְהַבַּיִת הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר הָיָה עֶלְיוֹן וְנוֹרָא אַף לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים
sources.says: Rashi explains it as "this house, which was high and awesome even to idol worshippers".

sources.quote: כמו היה עליון, עתיד במקום עבר
sources.says: Metzudat David says "will be high" means "was high", a future form used for the past.

sources.quote: וּבֵיתָא הָדֵין דַהֲוָה עִילָאֵי יְהֵי חֲרִיב
sources.says: The Targum renders "this house, which was high, will be destroyed".

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים יהיה חרב ויפרשו עליון לשון כריתה כמו כעלות גדיש בעתו
sources.says: Radak reports some who read עליון as a word for cutting off, so the house will be destroyed.

9:11.headline: Hiram "carried" Solomon: bore his costs, or raised him up
9:11.body: נשא means to lift or carry. Rashi says Hiram carried Solomon's load by supplying wood and gold. Ralbag says it may mean Hiram sent him supplies, or that he raised Solomon up by working for him.

sources.quote: עִנְיַן עֹמֶס, כִּלְכֵּל אֶת מַשָּׂאוֹ בְּדָבָר זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for a load: Hiram supplied Solomon's burden in this matter.

sources.quote: הוא מענין ארוחה ומשאת כטעם אם נשאת נשא לנו או יהיה הרצון בזה שהוא רומם ונשא בזה את שלמה
sources.says: Ralbag says it means provisions and gifts, or else that Hiram raised Solomon up by this.

9:13.headline: Hiram names the towns כבול, "fettered land"
9:13.body: Hiram did not like the towns and named them כבול. Rashi links it to כבלים, chains: mud where the foot sinks and is held fast. Radak says it means closed, so poor that no one traveled through, and Ralbag says it was sand that bore no fruit.

sources.quote: אֶרֶץ כְּבָלִים, אֶרֶץ טִיט, שֶׁהָרֶגֶל מִשְׁתַּקֵעַ וְנִכְבֶּלֶת בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a land of chains, a land of mud where the foot sinks and is held.

sources.quote: כבול. מלשון (תהלים קמט ח) בכבלי ברזל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says כבול comes from "iron chains" in Psalm 149:8.

sources.quote: סגור שלא היו עוברים ושבים שם מגריעות הארץ
sources.says: Radak says it means closed: no one passed through because the land was so poor.

sources.quote: ארץ חול שאינה עושה פירות
sources.says: Ralbag says it means a sandy land that bears no fruit.

9:15.headline: Why a place in Jerusalem was called the Millo, "the filling"
9:15.body: מלוא comes from the word for filling. Rashi says the place had a low wall around it and was filled in with earth. Ralbag says it was where Israel gathered, and reads the name like the phrase קראו מלאו, "call out, gather".

sources.quote: וְנִקְרָא מִלּוֹא, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמֻּקָּף חוֹמָה נְמוּכָה, וּמִלְּאוּ לְתוֹכָהּ עָפָר
sources.says: Rashi says it was called Millo because a low wall surrounded it and they filled it with earth.

sources.quote: והוא המקום שהיו נאספים שם ישראל ולזה נקרא מלוא כטעם קראו מלאו
sources.says: Ralbag says it was the place where Israel gathered, so it was called Millo, as in "call out, gather".

9:24.headline: "Only" Pharaoh's daughter: a hint at Solomon's fault
9:24.body: Rashi reports a reading that אך, "only", marks a wrong. Solomon built over the Millo, an open space his father had left for pilgrims, for Pharaoh's daughter. Rashi's own reading: the Millo was built only because her house stood next to it.

sources.quote: וְזֶהוּ 'אַךְ' הָאָמוּר כָּאן, אַךְ בְּזוֹ הֶעֱוָה שְׁלֹמֹה, שֶׁבָּנָה לָהּ אֶת הַמִּלּוֹא, כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי
sources.says: Rashi says he heard that this "only" means: in this Solomon did wrong, that he built the Millo for her.

sources.quote: אָבִיךָ הִנִּיחוֹ פָּרוּץ לְעוֹלֵי רְגָלִים
sources.says: Rashi says Jeroboam rebuked Solomon: your father left it open for the pilgrims.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא שֶׁבַּת פַּרְעֹה עָלְתָה אֶל בֵּיתָהּ, וְהַמִּלּוֹא סָמוּךְ לְאוֹתוֹ בַּיִת, אָז בָּנָה אֶת הַמִּלּוֹא
sources.says: Rashi's own reading is that he built the Millo only because Pharaoh's daughter moved to her house, which was next to it.

9:25.headline: אתו: burning incense "with it" or "on it"
9:25.body: אתו usually means "with it". Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as "on it", the gold incense altar. Radak also gives the plain sense: he burned incense on the other altar, the one that went with the first.

sources.quote: והקטיר אתו. כמו עליו
sources.says: Radak says אתו here means "on it".

sources.quote: או פי' אתו כמשמעו ולפי שזכר כי העלה עולות על המזבח האחר
sources.says: Radak says it may also mean "with it" in its plain sense, pointing to the other altar mentioned with the first.

sources.quote: אתו. עם המזבח, רוצה לומר: עליו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means with the altar, that is, on it.

9:26.headline: ואני is not "and I" here, but a fleet of ships
9:26.body: אני here is not the word for "I". Rashi says it means a ship. Malbim says it is a group word for many ships, the way "I have an ox and a donkey" means many animals.

sources.quote: וָאֳנִי. אֳנִיָּה
sources.says: Rashi says אני means a ship.

sources.quote: ואני הוא שם הכלל אניות, כמו ויהי לי שור וחמור
sources.says: Malbim says אני is a collective word for ships, like "I have ox and donkey".

sources.quote: וּסְפִינָתָא עֲבַד שְׁלֹמֹה מַלְכָּא
sources.says: The Targum renders it "King Solomon made a ship".
